definition_zh: 对整机或系统中的单个零件、元件进行形状、尺寸、材料与公差设计的工作
definition_en: the work of specifying the shape, size, material and tolerances of a single part or element within a machine or system
core_image: 屏幕上放大一个轴承座，孔径、壁厚与配合公差层层标注，零件在整台机器中的位置被虚线框出
scene: 设计室里，工程师在屏幕上放大一个轴承座，标注孔径与公差。 Good component design keeps repair costs low.
sceneCN: 这里指对单个零件做尺寸、材料与公差设计的工作（第 1 个义项：对整机或系统中的单个零件、元件进行形状、尺寸、材料与公差设计的工作）；句意：良好的零部件设计能压低维修成本。

senses.title: Designing one part of a whole
senses.titleCN: 为整体中的一个零件做设计
senses.definition: the work of defining a single part that will be assembled with others
senses.definitionCN: 定义一个将与其他零件装配在一起的单个零件的工作
senses.example: Good component design begins with the loads the part must carry.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的零部件设计从零件必须承担的荷载开始。
senses.why: Component names one element of a larger whole and design names the planning, so the phrase is planning a part in its context.
senses.whyCN: 「部件」指更大整体中的一个元素，「设计」指规划，因此这个词组是在整体背景中规划一个零件。

senses.title: Shape and sizing
senses.definition: the choice of geometry, wall thickness and section that gives the part its strength
senses.definitionCN: 选择使零件获得强度的几何形状、壁厚与截面
senses.example: Component design reduced the bracket's weight without weakening it.
senses.exampleCN: 零部件设计减轻了支架重量而没有削弱它。
senses.why: A part carries load through its shape, so geometry is the first decision of the work.
senses.whyCN: 零件靠形状承载，因此几何是这项工作的第一个决定。

senses.title: Material and process choice
senses.definition: the selection of metal, plastic or composite and of casting, machining or moulding
senses.definitionCN: 选择金属、塑料或复合材料，以及铸造、机加工或模压等工艺
senses.example: Component design chose cast aluminium because the shape was complex.
senses.exampleCN: 零部件设计因形状复杂而选择了铸铝。
senses.why: Shape and material must be decided together, because some shapes can only be made by some processes.
senses.whyCN: 形状与材料必须一起决定，因为某些形状只能由某些工艺做出。

senses.title: Tolerance and fit
senses.definition: the allowed variation in size and the clearance or interference between mating parts
senses.definitionCN: 允许的尺寸偏差以及配合件之间的间隙或过盈
senses.example: Component design set a tight tolerance on the shaft bore.
senses.exampleCN: 零部件设计给轴孔定了很紧的公差。
senses.why: Parts made separately must still meet, so the work states how much variation is acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 分开制造的零件仍要能配合，因此这项工作要规定允许多大偏差。

senses.title: Electronic component design
senses.definition: the design of a resistor, capacitor, chip or connector as a unit inside a circuit
senses.definitionCN: 设计电路中的电阻、电容、芯片或连接器等单元
senses.example: Component design for the board had to fit a smaller case.
senses.exampleCN: 这块电路板的元件设计必须装进更小的外壳。
senses.why: The word component also names circuit elements, so the phrase extends from machine parts to electronics.
senses.whyCN: 「部件」一词也指电路元件，因此这个词组从机械零件扩展到电子。

senses.title: Design for manufacture
senses.definition: the adjustment of a part so that it can be made, assembled and inspected economically
senses.definitionCN: 调整零件使其能被经济地制造、装配与检验
senses.example: Component design removed the deep pocket that slowed machining.
senses.exampleCN: 零部件设计去掉了那个拖慢加工的深腔。
senses.why: A part that cannot be made cheaply is a failed design, so the work must respect the factory.
senses.whyCN: 不能便宜制造的零件就是失败的设计，因此这项工作必须顾及工厂条件。

senses.title: Modularity and interfaces
senses.definition: the definition of how a part connects to its neighbours, including dimensions, plugs and mounting points
senses.definitionCN: 规定零件如何与相邻件连接，包括尺寸、插接件与安装点
senses.example: Component design fixed the mounting points before the frame was drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 零部件设计在画框架之前就定下了安装点。
senses.why: Every part has neighbours, so the work also defines the interfaces it must honour.
senses.whyCN: 每个零件都有邻居，因此这项工作还要定义它必须遵守的接口。

senses.title: Verification and revision
senses.definition: the testing, stress checking and redesign that follows a first part drawing
senses.definitionCN: 首版零件图之后的试验、应力校核与重新设计
senses.example: Component design went through three revisions after the vibration test.
senses.exampleCN: 振动试验之后，零部件设计经历了三次改版。
senses.why: A drawing is a proposal until it is tested, so the work ends in verification and revision.
senses.whyCN: 图纸在被验证之前只是提案，因此这项工作以验证与改型收尾。

intro.en: Component design joins a Latin word for something placed together with a Latin word for marking out; the phrase is about planning one element of a larger machine.
intro.cn: 「零部件设计」把拉丁语中表示「一起放置之物」的词，与拉丁语表示「标出」的词组合；这个词组讲的是规划一台大机器中的一个元素。

items.en: Ponere meant to place or put; its perfect participle positum supplied many English words about placing and position.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语动词指放置、安置；它的完成分词为许多表示「放置」与「位置」的英语词提供了成分。

items.en: The prefix com-, meaning together, produced componere, to put together, and componens named the thing that is put in with others.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的前缀构成了「放在一起」的动词，其分词名词指被放进整体中的东西。

items.en: English took component from the participle, naming one element of a larger assembly rather than the whole.
items.cn: 英语从该分词取得「部件」一词，命名大装配体中的一个元素，而不是整体。

items.en: Signum meant a mark or sign, and designare meant to mark out or plan something by signs.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词指标记或符号，相应的动词表示用符号标出或规划。

items.en: Design entered English through French and Italian uses meaning a plan or a drawing, then narrowed to the act of planning a product.
items.cn: 「设计」经法语与意大利语的用法进入英语，原指计划或图样，后来缩小为规划产品的行为。

items.en: Mass production made it necessary to plan each part against its neighbours, and the two words became a fixed phrase for that work.
items.cn: 批量生产使人们必须对照相邻件来规划每个零件，这两个词便固定成指这项工作的词组。

note.en: The first group shares the placing root; the second group names related planning words.
note.cn: 第一组共享「放置」词根；第二组是相关的规划用语。

entries.definition: The stage after concept design when every part is fixed; broader than one component.

entries.definition: The design of the whole sellable item, including form and user experience.
entries.definitionCN: 整个可售物品的设计，包括外形与使用体验。

definition_zh: 累积的；渐增的；累计的
definition_en: increasing by successive additions, or resulting from a total built up over time
core_image: 沙漏下方的沙堆一层层加高
scene: 这组词中， The cumulative effect of small emissions became visible after a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 cumulative 是「累积的」（第 2 个义项：多次小影响累加成的总效应）；句意：微小排放的累积效应十年后才显现出来。图中可辨识物件：沙漏、逐年排放柱状图、上升曲线、工厂烟囱、十年刻度。

pos.zh: 累积的；渐增的；累计的（常作定语）

senses.title: Growing by successive additions
senses.titleCN: 逐次累加的：一层压一层地增长
senses.definition: increasing as each new amount is added to what already exists
senses.definitionCN: 随着每一新量加到既有数量上而增长
senses.example: The cumulative growth of the archive surprised the librarians.
senses.exampleCN: 档案的累积增长让馆员们感到意外。
senses.why: Latin cumulare means 'to heap up', from cumulus 'heap'. The adjective describes anything built by adding layer upon layer rather than by one jump.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 cumulare 意为“堆起”，来自 cumulus“堆”。这个形容词描述任何靠一层层添加、而非一步跳升而形成的事物。

senses.title: The total effect of many small causes
senses.titleCN: 累积效应：小事重复造成的总后果
senses.definition: describing an effect produced by repeated small causes acting over time
senses.definitionCN: 指由重复的小原因长期作用所产生的效应
senses.example: The cumulative effect of small emissions became visible after a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 微小排放的累积效应十年后才显现出来。
senses.why: A single small cause may be harmless, but heaping them together crosses a threshold, so the adjective names the total rather than any one item.
senses.whyCN: 单个小原因也许无害，但把它们堆起来就会越过某个阈值，因此这个形容词命名的是总体，而非任何单项。

senses.title: A running total in statistics
senses.titleCN: 累计数：统计里一路加下去的和
senses.definition: in statistics, describing a total formed by adding each value in turn
senses.definitionCN: 统计中把每个数值依次相加形成的总数
senses.example: The cumulative frequency column reaches one hundred per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 累积频数列最终达到百分之百。
senses.why: The statistical sense makes the heap exact: each row adds one more item to the pile, and the column shows the pile at every step.
senses.whyCN: 统计义把“堆”精确化：每一行往堆上再加一项，整列显示每一步的堆积高度。

senses.title: Cumulative evidence in law
senses.titleCN: 累积证据：多条单独不足、合起来有力
senses.definition: in law, describing separate pieces of evidence that strengthen one another when taken together
senses.definitionCN: 法律中指多条证据合在一起时互相增强
senses.example: The court admitted the records as cumulative evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院将这些记录作为累积证据采纳。
senses.why: Each item adds weight rather than replacing the others; the legal sense treats proof as a heap that grows heavier with every piece.
senses.whyCN: 每一项都在增加分量，而非替代其他项；法律义把证明看成一堆越加越重的东西。

senses.title: Cumulative interest or dividend
senses.titleCN: 累积利息／股息：未付部分滚存
senses.definition: in finance, describing interest or dividends that accumulate and must be paid later
senses.definitionCN: 金融中指利息或股息累积起来、须在以后支付
senses.example: The preferred shares carry cumulative dividends.
senses.exampleCN: 这些优先股带累积股息。
senses.why: Money that is not paid now is heaped onto the next payment, so the finance sense is the literal heap transferred from sand to unpaid amounts.
senses.whyCN: 现在未付的钱被堆到下一次支付上，因此金融义就是把沙堆的字面意象转移到未付金额。

senses.title: Lifetime accumulated risk
senses.titleCN: 累积风险：一生中反复暴露的总账
senses.definition: in medicine and public health, describing risk that adds up over repeated or prolonged exposure
senses.definitionCN: 医学与公共卫生中指重复或长期暴露累加起来的风险
senses.example: Cumulative exposure to sunlight raises the risk of skin damage.
senses.exampleCN: 长期累积的日晒会增加皮肤损伤风险。
senses.why: Risk is measured over a lifetime, not a single day: each exposure adds a small amount to the total, so the adjective marks the sum rather than the episode.
senses.whyCN: 风险按一生而非单日衡量：每次暴露都在总量上加一点，因此形容词标记的是总和，而非单次事件。

senses.title: Accumulated damage in materials
senses.titleCN: 累积损伤：材料一次次受载后的总损耗
senses.definition: in engineering, describing damage that builds up through repeated stress
senses.definitionCN: 工程中指反复受力逐步积累的损伤
senses.example: Engineers track cumulative damage in the turbine blades.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师追踪涡轮叶片的累积损伤。
senses.why: Materials do not fail from one load but from many; the adjective names the damage that has been heaped up beyond the visible single event.
senses.whyCN: 材料不是因一次载荷失效，而是因多次载荷失效；这个形容词命名的正是超出单次可见事件的堆积损伤。

senses.title: Cumulative culture
senses.titleCN: 累积文化：一代代叠加改进
senses.definition: in anthropology, describing knowledge or technology that improves through repeated additions across generations
senses.definitionCN: 人类学中指知识或技术经代际反复添补而改进
senses.example: Cumulative culture allows each generation to start from earlier tools.
senses.exampleCN: 累积文化让每一代人都从更早的工具出发。
senses.why: Culture is a heap that never resets: each generation adds a small improvement and passes the larger pile on, which is why human technology can outrun individual invention.
senses.whyCN: 文化是一堆不会清零的东西：每代添一点改进，再把更大的堆传下去，这正是人类技术能超越个人发明的原因。

intro.en: Cumulative is cumul- + -ive, from Latin cumulare 'to heap up'. The same stem gives accumulate and the cloud name cumulus, both built on the image of a pile.
intro.cn: cumulative 是 cumul- + -ive，来自拉丁 cumulare“堆起”。同一词干还产生 accumulate 与云名 cumulus，二者都建立在“堆”的意象上。

items.en: cumulus meant 'a heap, mass or pile'. It was used of piled earth or grain and later gave the meteorological term for heaped clouds.
items.cn: cumulus 意为“堆、堆块”。它曾用于堆起的土或谷物，后来产生指堆状云的气象术语。

items.en: cumulare 'to heap up, amass' was formed from cumulus. Its past participle cumulatus supplies the stem cumulat- used in English.
items.cn: cumulare“堆起、积聚”由 cumulus 构成。其过去分词 cumulatus 提供英语使用的词干 cumulat-。

items.en: The suffix -ive, from Latin -ivus 'having the nature of', makes an adjective of tendency: cumulative describes what tends to heap up or what results from heaping.
items.cn: 后缀 -ive 来自拉丁 -ivus“具有……性质的”，构成表倾向的形容词：cumulative 描述倾向于堆积的事物，或由堆积产生的结果。

items.en: English cumulative appears in the 17th century, first in learned and legal writing about totals and evidence. The date is approximate.
items.cn: 英语 cumulative 于17世纪出现，最早见于讨论总数与证据的学术和法律文本。年代为约数。

items.en: Statistics, finance, medicine and engineering each adopted the word for their own running totals in the 19th and 20th centuries.
items.cn: 统计学、金融、医学与工程分别在19、20世纪采用这个词来表示各自的累计总量。

items.en: The deeper origin of Latin cumulus is uncertain; it is often treated as a derivative of a root meaning 'heap', but no single reconstruction is agreed. Exact English dates are approximate.
items.cn: 拉丁 cumulus 的更深来源不确定；常被视为某个意为“堆”的词根的派生，但没有公认的单一重构。英语确切年代为约数。

note.en: The first group contains look-alike words from different roots; the second contains words for totals and growth that count differently.
note.cn: 第一组是来自不同词根的形近词；第二组是计算方式不同的“总量／增长”类词。

entries.definition: Tending to accumulate; it stresses the habit or process of collecting, while cumulative usually describes the resulting total.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于积累的；强调收集的习惯或过程，而 cumulative 通常描述形成的总量。

entries.definition: A heap-shaped cloud; the noun names the pile itself, not the process of adding to it.
entries.definitionCN: 积云；这个名词命名堆本身，而非堆积过程。

entries.definition: Relating to a climax or highest point, from Latin culmen 'top'. It looks like cumulative but has no heap in it.
entries.definitionCN: 与顶点、高潮有关的，来自拉丁 culmen“顶”。它形似 cumulative，但词源里没有“堆”。

entries.definition: Already gathered into a store; it describes the completed stock, while cumulative describes the adding process or its pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 已经聚集起来的；描述完成的存量，而 cumulative 描述添加过程或其模式。

entries.definition: A total formed by combining separate items; it does not imply growth over time.
entries.definitionCN: 由各项合并而成的总数；不暗示随时间增长。

entries.definition: Increasing by small steps; it stresses the size of each step, while cumulative stresses the total reached.
entries.definitionCN: 逐步小幅增加的；强调每步的幅度，而 cumulative 强调达到的总量。

entries.definition: Shared by or belonging to a group; it is about ownership or joint action, not heaping over time.
entries.definitionCN: 由群体共享或属于群体的；关乎归属或共同行动，而非长期堆积。

entries.definition: Continuing step by step over time; it can describe growth but not necessarily a total.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间逐步持续的；可描述增长，但不必形成总量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin morphology, fixed collocations and the genuine cumulus family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实拉丁构词、固定搭配与真实的 cumulus 词族。

normal.en: cumulus 'heap' + -ive: the adjective describes whatever is formed by heaping.
normal.cn: cumulus“堆”+ -ive：这个形容词描述一切靠堆积形成的东西。

normal.en: accumulate and cumulative share the same heap, one as a verb and one as an adjective.
normal.cn: accumulate 与 cumulative 共享同一个“堆”，一个是动词，一个是形容词。

normal.en: Learn cumulative effect, cumulative total and cumulative evidence; these are the three most common academic uses.
normal.cn: 记住 cumulative effect、cumulative total、cumulative evidence；这是三个最常见的学术用法。

normal.en: cumulus clouds are heaps of cloud, which is the same picture as a cumulative total.
normal.cn: cumulus 云就是堆状的云，与累计总数的画面相同。

normal.en: Do not confuse cumulative with culminative: one heaps, the other reaches a top.
normal.cn: 不要把 cumulative 与 culminative 混淆：一个是堆，一个是到达顶点。

abstract.en: Picture sand falling through an hourglass, each grain adding to one growing cone.
abstract.cn: 想象沙粒穿过沙漏，每一粒都加到一个不断长高的圆锥上。

abstract.en: Picture a wall built one brick per day until it is thick enough to change the weather behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象每天只砌一块砖的墙，直到厚到足以改变墙后的天气。

abstract.en: Picture an interest ledger where unpaid amounts roll into the next row and grow larger each time.
abstract.cn: 想象一本利息账簿，未付金额滚入下一行，每次都变得更大。

examples.en: The cumulative total of donations passed one million dollars.
examples.cn: 捐款累计总额超过了一百万美元。

examples.en: Repeated small delays had a cumulative effect on the schedule.
examples.cn: 反复的小延误对进度产生了累积效应。

examples.en: The report assesses the cumulative impact of tourism on the coast.
examples.cn: 报告评估了旅游业对海岸的累积影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: “Q（cu）mulate（堆）”——像 Q 一样一圈圈堆上去 → cumulative 累积的、渐增的

root: 拉丁 cumulus“堆、堆块”→ cumulare“堆起、积聚”→ cumulat- 词干 + -ive“具有……性质的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one image: a heap that grows by addition. The heap may be sand, data, evidence, unpaid interest, exposure, damage or cultural knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个意象：靠添加而增高的堆。这堆东西可以是沙、数据、证据、未付利息、暴露量、损伤或文化知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cone of sand growing grain by grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：沙粒逐颗落下、不断长高的圆锥。

branches.en: ADDING: successive growth and a statistical running total are the same addition seen qualitatively and numerically.
branches.cn: 添加：逐次增长与统计累计数，是同一加法在性质与数量两个层面的呈现。

branches.en: THRESHOLD DAMAGE: small causes and repeated stress both become serious only after the heap is large enough.
branches.cn: 阈值损伤：小原因与反复应力，都要等堆足够大才变得严重。

branches.en: LAW AND FINANCE: separate evidence and unpaid dividends both add weight or value without replacing the earlier items.
branches.cn: 法律与金融：分散证据与未付股息都在增加分量或价值，而不取代先前项目。

branches.en: LIFETIME EXPOSURE: risk adds up across many episodes, so the total matters more than any single exposure.
branches.cn: 终生暴露：风险在多次事件中累加，因此总量比任何单次暴露更重要。

branches.en: CULTURE: improvements accumulate across generations, making the heap inherited rather than personal.
branches.cn: 文化：改进在代际间累积，使这堆东西成为继承物而非个人成就。

intro.en: Cumulative is a Latin adjective in -ive built on the participle stem cumulat-. The related verb accumulate adds the prefix ad- to the same base.
intro.cn: cumulative 是建立在分词词干 cumulat- 上的拉丁 -ive 形容词。相关动词 accumulate 在同一词基上加前缀 ad-。

latinIntro.en: Latin cumulus 'heap' gives cumulare 'to heap up' and the adjective cumulativus. English borrowed the stem as cumulat- and added -ive, while accumulate came through the prefixed form accumulare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cumulus“堆”产生 cumulare“堆起”与形容词 cumulativus。英语借入词干 cumulat- 并加 -ive，而 accumulate 经带前缀形式 accumulare 进入。

items.meaning: tending to heap up; formed by accumulation
items.meaningCN: 累积的；渐增的（cumulat- + -ive 表倾向）
items.example: The cumulative effect was larger than expected.

items.exampleCN: 灰尘在架子上积了起来。

items.meaning: a mass that has been gathered
items.meaningCN: 积累物；堆积（-ion 结果名词）
items.example: The accumulation of sediment blocked the channel.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物堆积堵塞了水道。

items.meaning: by adding one item to another
items.meaningCN: 累积地；渐增地（-ly 方式副词）
items.example: Cumulatively, the changes altered the whole system.
items.exampleCN: 这些变化累积起来改变了整个系统。

items.example: Cumulus clouds formed above the hills.

items.meaning: a device that stores energy or data
items.meaningCN: 蓄电池；累加器（-or 表装置）
items.example: The accumulator stores charge between cycles.
items.exampleCN: 蓄电池在循环之间储存电荷。

items.meaning: a running count of values up to a point
items.meaningCN: 累积频数（逐项累加的计数）
items.example: The cumulative frequency rises steadily across the table.
items.exampleCN: 累积频数在整张表中稳步上升。

items.meaning: separate proofs that reinforce one another
items.example: The judge described the letters as cumulative evidence.
items.exampleCN: 法官把这些信件称为累积证据。

items.meaning: tending to collect or pile up
items.meaningCN: 倾向于积累的（-ive 表倾向）
items.example: The accumulative habit of note-taking paid off.
items.exampleCN: 做笔记的积累习惯最终有了回报。

definition_zh: n. 烦恼；恼怒；令人厌烦的人或事
definition_en: The feeling of being mildly angry or irritated, or a person or thing that causes that feeling.
core_image: 一只在耳边绕圈的蚊子，赶不走
scene: 楼上装修的电钻声从早响到晚。 The noise from upstairs is a constant annoyance.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：这里不是指情绪，而是指「引起烦扰的东西」——楼上不断的电钻声本身就是一件烦扰。

forms.label: 复数（指具体烦扰事物时）

senses.title: The feeling of irritation
senses.definition: a mild anger caused by something troublesome or repeatedly disturbing
senses.definitionCN: 由麻烦或反复干扰之事引起的轻度怒气
senses.example: She could not hide her annoyance at the interruption.
senses.exampleCN: 她无法掩饰被打断时的恼火。
senses.why: The word descends from a Latin phrase meaning it is hateful to me, so the feeling is literally something made hateful to you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自一句意为「它令我憎恶」的拉丁语短语，所以这种情绪字面上就是「被弄成令你憎恶的东西」。

senses.title: The thing that irritates
senses.definition: a person, noise or habit that produces that feeling
senses.definitionCN: 产生这种感觉的人、噪声或习惯
senses.example: The dripping tap became a real annoyance.
senses.exampleCN: 那个滴水的水龙头成了真正的烦扰。
senses.why: English often turns a feeling noun into the name of its cause, and annoyance is a standard example: the noise is an annoyance.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把情绪名词转用为其原因的名称，annoyance 是典型例子：那噪声本身就是一件烦扰。

intro.en: Annoyance is built on annoy, which comes from Old French anui, from Late Latin inodiare, to make hateful, from the Latin phrase mihi in odio est, it is hateful to me.
intro.cn: annoyance 建立在 annoy 之上，annoy 来自古法语 anui，后者出自晚期拉丁语 inodiare「使可憎」，源于拉丁语短语 mihi in odio est「它令我憎恶」。

items.en: Latin odium meant hatred, and the phrase mihi in odio est meant it is hateful to me. The same root gives odious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 odium 意为「憎恨」，短语 mihi in odio est 意为「它令我憎恶」。同一词根产生 odious。

items.en: Late Latin inodiare turned that phrase into a verb meaning to make hateful, to trouble or offend.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 inodiare 把那句短语变成动词，意为「使可憎、使烦扰、冒犯」。

items.en: Old French anui and the verb anuier kept the sense of trouble, distress and irritation, and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语 anui 及动词 anuier 保留「烦扰、苦恼、恼怒」之义，并传入英语。

items.en: Middle English took the verb as anoyen in the thirteenth century, originally for serious harm as well as minor irritation.
items.cn: 中古英语在 13 世纪借为动词 anoyen，最初既指严重伤害，也指轻微烦扰。

items.en: Annoyance is formed with -ance, and English weakened the sense from harm to everyday irritation, then extended it to the cause.
items.cn: annoyance 用 -ance 构成，英语把含义从「伤害」弱化为日常「恼火」，再扩展到指引起恼火的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against noisome, which means foul-smelling, not noisy; the near-meaning group lists other words for irritation.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 noisome 混淆，它意为「恶臭的」而非「吵闹的」；近义组列出其他表示恼火的词。

entries.definition: To irritate or disturb.
entries.definitionCN: 使恼火或打扰。

entries.definition: Feeling mild anger.
entries.definitionCN: 感到轻度怒气的。

entries.definition: Causing mild anger.
entries.definitionCN: 引起轻度怒气的。

entries.definition: Foul-smelling or harmful, not noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 恶臭或有害的，不是吵闹的。

entries.definition: The state of being annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 被惹恼的状态。

entries.definition: A person or thing causing trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 引起麻烦的人或事。

entries.definition: The state of being worried and annoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 既担忧又恼火的状态。

entries.definition: Minor trouble or effort.
entries.definitionCN: 小小的麻烦或费心。

normalIntro.en: Annoyance is annoy plus -ance, and annoy comes from a Latin phrase about hatred, not from noise.
normalIntro.cn: annoyance 就是 annoy 加 -ance，而 annoy 来自一句关于「憎恶」的拉丁语短语，与 noise 无关。

normal.en: Uncountable for the feeling, countable for causes: an annoyance.
normal.cn: 指情绪时不可数，指原因时可数：an annoyance。

normal.en: Annoyed describes a person; annoying describes the cause.
normal.cn: annoyed 描述人，annoying 描述原因。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is to my annoyance, at the start of a clause.
normal.cn: 固定短语是 to my annoyance，放在句首。

normal.en: Annoy is not related to noise, despite the spelling.
normal.cn: 尽管拼写相近，annoy 与 noise 无关。

normal.en: Noisome means foul-smelling, so do not use it for loud.
normal.cn: noisome 意为「恶臭的」，不要用来表示吵闹。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito circling the ear at night.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚊子夜里在耳边绕圈。

abstract.en: Imagine a tap that drips once every four seconds.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每四秒滴一滴的水龙头。

abstract.en: Think of a small stone inside a shoe.
abstract.cn: 想象鞋里的一颗小石子。

examples.en: He sighed with annoyance and closed the window.
examples.cn: 他恼火地叹了口气，关上窗。

examples.en: The delay caused considerable annoyance to passengers.
examples.cn: 延误让乘客相当恼火。

examples.en: Parking fines are a daily annoyance in this street.
examples.cn: 在这条街上，停车罚单是每天的烦扰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「额诺伊恩斯」——额（an）诺（noy）伊恩斯（ance）：额头上冒火，耳边「嗡嗡」赶不走，就是烦恼、烦扰。

root: 拉丁语 odium「憎恨」经短语 in odio「令我憎恶」生出晚期拉丁语 inodiare，古法语作 anui，英语作 annoy「使恼火」，加 -ance 成 annoyance，兼指情绪与起因。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one small hatred: the feeling inside you, and the noise or habit outside that puts it there.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一点小小的憎恶：你心里的那种感觉，以及外面把它放进来的噪声或习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mosquito circling the ear that will not be driven off
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在耳边绕圈赶不走的蚊子

branches.en: A sigh at the third interruption.
branches.cn: 第三次被打断时的一声叹气。

branches.en: Irritation that never quite becomes anger.
branches.cn: 始终没变成愤怒的恼火。

branches.en: A drill that starts at seven each morning.
branches.cn: 每早七点开工的电钻。

branches.en: A tap dripping through the night.
branches.cn: 整夜滴水的水龙头。

branches.en: One feeling and the thing that makes it.
branches.cn: 一种情绪，以及造成它的东西。

intro.en: Annoyance is annoy plus -ance, and the same noy- root builds noisome, while vex- and ir- build the synonyms.
intro.cn: annoyance 是 annoy 加 -ance，同一个 noy- 词根还构成 noisome，而 vex- 与 ir- 构成它的近义词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is odium, hatred, turned into the verb inodiare; Old French anui carried it into English annoy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 odium「憎恨」，被变成动词 inodiare；古法语 anui 把它带入英语 annoy。

latinEntries.exampleCN: inodiare 是 annoy 的来源。
anui 传入英语成为 annoy。

definition_zh: 恐高症；高处恐惧
definition_en: an unusually strong and persistent fear of heights
core_image: 站在高台边缘，双腿发软，不敢往下看
scene: 观景台的玻璃地板前，游客扶着栏杆，迟迟不敢迈出一步。 Her acrophobia kept her far from the glass edge.
sceneCN: 这里 acrophobia 是「恐高症」（第 1 个义项：对高处的强烈恐惧）；句意为她的恐高症让她远离玻璃边缘。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「恐高的；恐高症相关的」
由本词去掉 -ia 加 -e 构成，义为「恐高者」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「以恐高的方式」

senses.title: Fear of heights
senses.definition: a strong fear of being high up or of looking down from a height
senses.definitionCN: 对身处高处或从高处向下看的强烈恐惧
senses.example: His acrophobia made the ferris wheel a trial rather than a treat.
senses.exampleCN: 他的恐高症让摩天轮成了一种折磨而不是享受。
senses.why: Greek akron means top or height and phobos means fear, so the word is literally height-fear.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 akron 意为「顶端、高处」，phobos 意为「恐惧」，所以这个词字面上就是「高处恐惧」。

senses.title: A clinical phobia
senses.definition: a diagnosable anxiety disorder in which the fear is out of proportion and leads to avoidance
senses.definitionCN: 一种可诊断的焦虑障碍，恐惧程度与危险不相称并导致回避
senses.example: The clinic treats acrophobia as an anxiety disorder, not a character flaw.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把恐高症当作焦虑障碍来治疗，而不是性格缺陷。
senses.why: Once the fear is persistent and disabling, it moves from a common feeling into a clinical category.
senses.whyCN: 当恐惧持续并造成功能损害，它就从常见感受变成临床分类。

senses.title: Physical symptoms
senses.definition: the bodily reactions triggered by heights, such as dizziness, sweating, trembling and a racing heart
senses.definitionCN: 高处引发的身体反应，如头晕、出汗、发抖与心跳加快
senses.example: Her acrophobia showed itself as sweating palms before she even reached the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 她的恐高症在她还没走到阳台时就表现为掌心出汗。
senses.why: Fear prepares the body to escape, so the word also names the physical alarm that comes with the height.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧让身体准备逃离，所以这个词也指随高处而来的身体警报。

senses.title: Trigger situations
senses.definition: places and activities that set off the fear, such as balconies, ladders, bridges and tall buildings
senses.definitionCN: 引发恐惧的场所与活动，如阳台、梯子、桥和高楼
senses.example: Glass floors are a common trigger for acrophobia.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃地板是恐高症常见的触发情境。
senses.why: The fear needs a cue, and modern buildings supply many cues that make the height visible.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧需要一个线索，而现代建筑提供了许多让高度变得可见的线索。

senses.title: Exposure therapy
senses.definition: treatment that reduces the fear by gradual, controlled contact with heights
senses.definitionCN: 通过逐步、受控地接触高处来减轻恐惧的治疗
senses.example: The therapist used exposure therapy for her acrophobia, starting with a low step.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师用暴露疗法治疗她的恐高症，从一级矮台阶开始。
senses.why: If avoidance keeps the fear alive, controlled approach is the treatment, so the word appears in therapy contexts.
senses.whyCN: 如果回避让恐惧持续，受控的接近就是治疗，所以这个词出现在治疗语境中。

senses.title: Virtual reality treatment
senses.definition: therapy that uses simulated heights in virtual reality to practise coping safely
senses.definitionCN: 利用虚拟现实中的模拟高处，在安全环境中练习应对的治疗
senses.example: The clinic offers acrophobia sessions in a virtual glass lift.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在虚拟玻璃电梯里提供恐高症治疗课程。
senses.why: Simulation gives the height without the danger, which makes it a modern tool for the same old fear.
senses.whyCN: 模拟提供高度却不提供危险，于是它成了对付这种古老恐惧的现代工具。

senses.title: Distinction from vertigo
senses.definition: the difference between fear of heights and vertigo, which is a false sense of spinning
senses.definitionCN: 对高处的恐惧与眩晕的区别，后者是一种虚假的旋转感
senses.example: Acrophobia is about danger, while vertigo is about the room seeming to move.
senses.exampleCN: 恐高症关乎危险，而眩晕关乎房间似乎在移动。
senses.why: Two experiences can occur together, so clinical language keeps the fear and the spinning sensation separate.
senses.whyCN: 两种体验可能同时出现，所以临床语言把「恐惧」与「旋转感」分开命名。

senses.title: Everyday height anxiety
senses.definition: a mild, common unease around heights that does not amount to a disorder
senses.definitionCN: 在高处附近轻度而常见的紧张感，尚未达到障碍程度
senses.example: He calls it acrophobia, though he still climbs ladders when he must.
senses.exampleCN: 他称之为恐高症，尽管必要时他仍会爬梯子。
senses.why: People borrow the clinical word for ordinary unease, a common looseness in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 人们借临床词汇来形容普通的紧张感，这是日常语言中常见的宽松用法。

intro.en: Acrophobia is a Greek-derived compound made in modern medical English from words for height and fear.
intro.cn: acrophobia 是用希腊语「高处」与「恐惧」两词在现代医学英语中构成的复合词。

items.en: Akron meant the top, tip or highest point; it is also the source of acrobat and acropolis.
items.cn: akron 意为「顶端、尖端、最高点」，也是 acrobat 与 acropolis 的来源。

items.en: Phobos meant fear or panic and was also the name of a deity of fright.
items.cn: phobos 意为「恐惧、惊慌」，也是希腊神话中惊恐之神的名字。

items.en: The suffix -phobia formed words for abnormal fear in Greek medical writing.
items.cn: 后缀 -phobia 在希腊医学文献中构成表示异常恐惧的词。

items.en: Scientific Latin coined acrophobia from akron and -phobia; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语用 akron 与 -phobia 造出 acrophobia，确切首次使用时间不确定。

items.en: The word entered English medical writing in the nineteenth century as phobias were being classified.
items.cn: 十九世纪恐惧症被分类时，这个词进入英语医学文献。

items.en: It now appears in everyday speech as well, often for mild unease rather than a diagnosis.
items.cn: 如今它也出现在日常口语中，常指轻度不适而非临床诊断。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -phobia words built on Greek roots; the near-meaning group gathers balance and anxiety terms with different mechanisms.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以希腊词根构成的 -phobia 词；近义组收机制不同的平衡与焦虑类词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning afraid of heights or relating to acrophobia.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恐高的」或「与恐高症相关的」。

entries.definition: A person who fears heights.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐高者」。

entries.definition: Fear of open or crowded places; it shares the -phobia suffix but a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广场恐惧症」，共享 -phobia 后缀但词根不同。

entries.definition: Fear of enclosed spaces; a parallel formation with a different first element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幽闭恐惧症」，是替换首元素的平行构词。

entries.definition: A performer who moves high above the ground; it shares akron, height, but not phobos.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杂技演员」，共享 akron「高处」词根，但不含 phobos。

entries.definition: A false sensation of spinning or movement; a balance symptom, not a fear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「眩晕」，是虚假的旋转或移动感，属平衡症状而非恐惧。

entries.definition: The general emotion of danger; broad and not tied to heights.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐惧」，是一般危险情绪，范围宽泛且不限于高处。

entries.definition: A general state of worry; acrophobia is a focused, situation-specific form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焦虑」，是一般担忧状态；恐高症是聚焦于特定情境的形式。

entries.definition: A clinical phrase for discomfort at heights that may fall short of a full phobia.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「高度不耐受」，指未达到完整恐惧症程度的高处不适。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real akron and phobos roots and the clinical phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 akron 与 phobos 词根，以及这个词实际出现的临床搭配。

normal.en: Akron is the top or tip, so acro- words are about the highest point.
normal.cn: akron 是顶端或尖端，所以 acro- 开头的词都与最高点有关。

normal.en: Phobos is fear, the same element in agoraphobia and claustrophobia.
normal.cn: phobos 是恐惧，同一元素也出现在 agoraphobia 与 claustrophobia 中。

normal.en: Acrobat shares the height root but has no fear in it.
normal.cn: acrobat 共享「高处」词根，但其中没有「恐惧」。

normal.en: Acrophobia is a diagnosable anxiety disorder when the fear is persistent and disabling.
normal.cn: 当恐惧持续并造成功能损害时，acrophobia 是可诊断的焦虑障碍。

normal.en: Exposure therapy works by replacing avoidance with controlled approach.
normal.cn: 暴露疗法用受控接近取代回避，从而起作用。

abstract.en: Picture a glass floor: the eyes see solid surface, but the legs refuse to believe it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块玻璃地板：眼睛看见实心表面，双腿却拒绝相信。

abstract.en: The fear lives in the gap between the body and the drop, a gap the mind fills with falling.
abstract.cn: 恐惧住在身体与落差之间的缝隙里，而想象用「坠落」填满了这道缝隙。

abstract.en: Acrophobia is not the height itself but the story the body tells about the height.
abstract.cn: 恐高症不是高度本身，而是身体关于高度讲的那个故事。

examples.en: Acrophobia stopped her from taking the job on the twentieth floor.
examples.cn: 恐高症使她无法接受那份位于二十层的工作。

examples.en: The study found that virtual reality can reduce acrophobia in a few sessions.
examples.cn: 研究发现虚拟现实能在几次课程内减轻恐高症。

examples.en: He described his acrophobia as a sudden urge to step back from any edge.
examples.cn: 他把自己的恐高症描述为一种突然想从任何边缘退后的冲动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克罗福比阿」——阿克罗站在高处，福气比阿谁少，腿却先软：恐高症

root: 希腊语 akron「顶端、高处」与 phobos「恐惧」组合，经科学拉丁语构成 acrophobia；后缀 -phobia 表示异常恐惧。akron 也是 acrobat 与 acropolis 的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses move from the plain fear of heights to its clinical status, bodily symptoms, triggers, treatments, its difference from vertigo, and its loose everyday use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从对高处的直接恐惧，延伸到临床地位、身体症状、触发情境、治疗方式、与眩晕的区别，以及日常的宽泛用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stands at a glass edge, legs trembling, unable to look down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在玻璃边缘，双腿发抖，不敢向下看。

branches.en: THE FEELING: from a plain fear of heights to mild everyday unease.
branches.cn: 感受线：从直接的高处恐惧到日常轻度不适。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: persistent fear becomes a diagnosis with bodily symptoms.
branches.cn: 临床线：持续的恐惧变成带有身体症状的诊断。

branches.en: THE CUE: balconies, ladders and glass floors make height visible.
branches.cn: 线索线：阳台、梯子与玻璃地板让高度变得可见。

branches.en: THE CURE: exposure and simulation teach the body a safer story.
branches.cn: 治疗线：暴露与模拟教给身体一个更安全的故事。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: fear of heights is kept distinct from the spinning of vertigo.
branches.cn: 边界线：把高处恐惧与眩晕的旋转感区分开。

intro.en: The word is two Greek elements plus a Greek-derived suffix, assembled in scientific Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个希腊语元素加一个源自希腊语的后缀组成，在科学拉丁语中装配。

latinIntro.en: Greek akron and phobos are recorded; the compound acrophobia belongs to modern scientific Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 akron 与 phobos 均有记录；复合词 acrophobia 属现代科学拉丁语。

items.example: It forms acrophobia and many clinical terms.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acrophobia 以及许多临床术语。

items.example: It is the fear element behind -phobia.
items.exampleCN: 它是 -phobia 背后的「恐惧」元素。

items.example: It is the height element behind acro-.
items.exampleCN: 它是 acro- 背后的「高处」元素。

items.example: It forms agoraphobia, a parallel phobia.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agoraphobia，一种平行的恐惧症。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「恐高的」
由本词去掉 -ia 加 -e 构成，义为「恐高者」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「以恐高的方式」

definition_zh: 有共情力的；体察他人处境的；善解人意的；同理式的；移情的；令人代入的；体谅的；以用户感受为中心的
definition_en: able to understand and share what another person is feeling
core_image: 一个人听人说话时，眉毛先于对方皱了起来
scene: 会议里有人低声说家里出了事，坐在斜对面的同事没有追问，只把会议记录推到一边。 When a colleague mentioned a family emergency in a low voice, the woman across the table said nothing and quietly moved the minutes aside, an empathetic response.
sceneCN: 这里 empathetic 指「体察他人处境的回应」（第 2 个义项：以举动体现对他人感受的理解）；句意为同事低声提到家中急事，斜对面的女士没有追问，只把会议记录推到一边，这便是体察他人处境的回应。可辨识物件：会议桌、记录本、推开的动作、压低的声音。

pos.zh: 有共情力的；体察他人处境的；善解人意的；同理式的；移情的；令人代入的；体谅的；以用户感受为中心的

collocations.zh: 以用户感受为中心的设计

senses.title: A person who feels with others
senses.definition: of a person, readily understanding and sharing the feelings of others
senses.definitionCN: 指人容易理解并分担他人的感受
senses.example: She is the most empathetic person in the department.
senses.exampleCN: 她是部门里最有共情力的人。
senses.why: The adjective moves the noun onto a person: empathy is the capacity, and empathetic says that someone has it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把名词移到人身上：empathy 是能力，empathetic 则说明某人拥有这种能力。

senses.title: A reply that fits the feeling
senses.titleCN: 与对方感受相称的回应
senses.definition: of a response or action, showing that another's feeling has been understood
senses.definitionCN: 指回应或举动显示已理解对方的感受
senses.example: His empathetic reply was to sit down and say nothing for a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回应是坐下来，先沉默片刻，这正体察了对方的感受。
senses.why: A response can demonstrate understanding even when no words are offered, which is why the adjective often describes actions.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有言语，回应也能显示理解，因此这个形容词常用来描述动作。

senses.title: A temperament that notices
senses.definition: having a temperament that notices and cares about others' states
senses.definitionCN: 具有留意并关心他人状态的性格
senses.example: The nurses described him as empathetic and unhurried.
senses.exampleCN: 护士们说他善解人意，而且从不急躁。
senses.why: Temperament is the standing version of a single act: what someone does once, an empathetic person does by habit.
senses.whyCN: 性格是单次行为的持久版本：某人偶一为之的事，善解人意者会习惯性地去做。

senses.title: Listening that gives room
senses.definition: of a way of listening that leaves the speaker room to finish
senses.definitionCN: 指一种让说话者把话说完的倾听方式
senses.example: Her empathetic listening kept him talking when he might have stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 她共情式的倾听让他在本可能停下时继续说了下去。
senses.why: The word can describe technique as well as feeling, because listening has a form that can be learned.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可描述感受，也可描述技巧，因为倾听有一种可以学会的形式。

senses.title: The clinical sense
senses.definition: in psychology, relating to the practitioner's entry into another's experience
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，指从业者进入他人体验的做法
senses.example: The training stresses an empathetic stance rather than quick interpretation.
senses.exampleCN: 培训强调共情的立场，而非急于作出解释。
senses.why: Clinical writing needed an adjective for the trained stance, and chose this one over the older variant.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作需要一个形容词来指受训后的立场，于是选用了这个较新的变体。

senses.title: Work that holds the viewer
senses.definition: of a story or image, drawing the audience into a character's feeling
senses.definitionCN: 指故事或影像把观众带入角色的感受
senses.example: The documentary is empathetic without ever becoming sentimental.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片让人代入，却从不流于感伤。
senses.why: Art can lend feeling without claiming it, and criticism uses the adjective for that loan.
senses.whyCN: 艺术可以借出感受而不将其据为己有，评论便用这个形容词指这种出借。

senses.title: Considerate under pressure
senses.definition: showing consideration for someone in a difficult position
senses.definitionCN: 对处境困难者表现出体贴
senses.example: The manager was empathetic about the deadline and moved it by a week.
senses.exampleCN: 经理对截止期限的处理很体谅，把它往后挪了一周。
senses.why: Consideration becomes visible when a rule is bent for a person, and the adjective covers that small bend.
senses.whyCN: 当规则为某个人稍作弯折时，体谅就变得可见，这个形容词正涵盖那一点弯折。

senses.title: Designed from the user's seat
senses.titleCN: 从使用者位置出发的设计
senses.definition: in design and service work, based on an understanding of users' experience
senses.definitionCN: 设计与服务工作中，建立在理解使用者体验之上
senses.example: The team ran an empathetic review of the complaint logs.
senses.exampleCN: 团队对投诉记录做了一次以用户感受为中心的复核。
senses.why: Design borrowed the word and made it a method: read the logs, sit in the chair, then build.
senses.whyCN: 设计借用了这个词并把它变成方法：读记录、坐进那把椅子，然后再动手。

intro.en: Empathetic is empathy plus the Greek adjective ending -etikos, and it competes with the older empathic. Empathy itself comes from Greek empatheia, from en- 'in' and pathos 'feeling'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: empathetic 是 empathy 加希腊形容词词尾 -etikos 构成，与更早的 empathic 并存。empathy 本身来自希腊 empatheia，由 en-「在内」与 pathos「感受」构成。下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Pathos meant what a person undergoes and the feeling it produces. Its deeper origin is generally thought to involve a root for suffering, but the form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: pathos 指人所经历的事以及由此产生的感受。其更深来源一般被认为与表示「受苦」的词根有关，但该形式属重构。

items.en: The noun entered English in the early twentieth century as a rendering of German aesthetic theory, then moved into psychology.
items.cn: 这个名词在二十世纪初进入英语，用以转译德国美学理论，随后进入心理学。

items.en: Empathic follows the shorter Greek pattern; empathetic follows the longer one and became common in clinical and general prose. Neither is wrong, and style guides differ.
items.cn: empathic 依循较短的希腊构词模式；empathetic 依循较长的模式，在临床与一般文章中更为常见。两者都不算错，各家体例偏好不同。

items.en: From counselling the adjective spread to management writing, art criticism and design, often before the response rather than the person.
items.cn: 这个形容词从心理咨询扩散到管理写作、艺术批评与设计，常放在「回应」之前而非「人」之前。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-history of pathos is a reconstruction, and the first English use of this adjective is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：pathos 的早期历史属重构，这个形容词的英语最早用例也无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms and two adjectives that look close but mean something else; group two holds words for understanding others' feelings.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形式，另加两个形近却另有含义的形容词；第二组是表示理解他人感受的词。

entries.definition: The capacity itself; empathetic describes a person or response that shows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身；empathetic 形容表现这种能力的人或回应。

entries.definition: The older and shorter adjective, common in clinical writing; the meaning is the same as empathetic.
entries.definitionCN: 更早、更短的形容词，常见于临床写作；含义与 empathetic 相同。

entries.definition: From Greek emphasis 'display', meaning forcefully stressed; it has no pathos and no feeling in its root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 emphasis「显示」，意为强调的；词根里既无 pathos，也无感受。

entries.definition: Built on pathos but means sadly inadequate or deserving pity; the prefix, not the root, separates it.
entries.definitionCN: 建在 pathos 上，却意为可怜、差劲；区分它的是前缀而非词根。

entries.definition: Feeling sorry for someone's trouble; empathetic implies sharing the feeling itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人的困境感到难过；empathetic 意味着共享那份感受本身。

entries.definition: Pity joined to a readiness to help; empathetic may stay with understanding.
entries.definitionCN: 怜悯并伴随帮助的意愿；empathetic 可能只停留在理解。

entries.definition: Able to see why someone acts as they do; empathetic adds the felt side.
entries.definitionCN: 能看出某人为何如此行事；empathetic 另添了感受的一面。

entries.definition: Quick to notice others' states, sometimes to one's own cost; empathetic stresses the sharing, not the noticing.
entries.definitionCN: 容易察觉他人状态，有时以自身为代价；empathetic 强调共享，而非察觉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek root of feeling, the two real adjective forms, and the real settings where the word is used.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「感受」词根、两个真实的形容词形式，以及这个词真实出现的场合。

normal.en: Empathy plus -etic gives the adjective, just as energy plus -etic gives energetic.
normal.cn: empathy 加 -etic 构成形容词，正如 energy 加 -etic 构成 energetic。

normal.en: Emphatic looks like this word but means forcefully stressed, so the two must be kept apart by their roots.
normal.cn: emphatic 字形相近却意为强调的，两者必须靠词根分清。

normal.en: The older empathic survives in clinical writing; empathetic is the common general form.
normal.cn: 较旧的 empathic 仍用于临床写作；empathetic 是常见的一般形式。

normal.en: It often sits before response, listening, approach and leader.
normal.cn: 它常放在回应、倾听、做法与领导者之前。

normal.en: The adverb empathetically marks how something is done, not what is felt.
normal.cn: 副词 empathetically 标示做事的方式，而非感受的内容。

abstract.en: Picture a brow that folds a moment before the speaker's does.
abstract.cn: 想象一道眉毛比说话者更早皱起。

abstract.en: Picture a notebook pushed aside without a word, because the note can wait.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记录本被无声地推到一边，因为记录可以等。

abstract.en: Picture a chair in a call centre occupied by a designer for one full shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一名设计师在呼叫中心的椅子上坐满一整班。

examples.en: An empathetic teacher notices the student who has stopped asking questions.
examples.cn: 有共情力的老师会注意到那个不再提问的学生。

examples.en: The report recommends a more empathetic approach to complaints.
examples.cn: 报告建议以更体察对方的方式处理投诉。

examples.en: Her empathetic silence gave him time to finish.
examples.cn: 她体谅的沉默给了他时间把话说完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「em（在内）+ pathetic（感受的）」——能走进别人感受里的 → 有共情力的

root: 希腊 empatheia（en-「在内」+ pathos「感受」）+ 形容词词尾 -etikos；与更早的 empathic 同义并存。pathos 更深词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one early frown: a person who feels with others, a reply that fits the feeling, a noticing temperament, listening that leaves room, a clinical stance, a work that holds the viewer, consideration under pressure, and design from the user's seat.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次提前皱起的眉展开：与他人同感的人、与感受相称的回应、善于察觉的性格、留出空间的倾听、临床立场、令人代入的作品、困境中的体谅，以及从使用者位置出发的设计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brow that folds a moment before the speaker's brow does.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道比说话者更早皱起的眉毛。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE TRAIT: someone who feels with others, and the temperament that makes it habitual.
branches.cn: 人与性格：与他人同感的人，以及使这件事成为习惯的性格。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE AND THE BEND: a reply that fits the feeling, and a rule moved for a person under pressure.
branches.cn: 回应与弯折：与感受相称的回应，以及为困境中的人挪动的规则。

branches.en: THE FORM OF LISTENING: silence that leaves the speaker room to finish.
branches.cn: 倾听的形式：让说话者把话说完的沉默。

branches.en: TRAINED AND BORROWED: the clinical stance, and the story that lends feeling to a viewer.
branches.cn: 受训与借出：临床立场，以及把感受借给观众的故事。

branches.en: DESIGNED FROM ANOTHER'S SEAT: a method that begins with the user's experience.
branches.cn: 从他人位置出发的设计：以使用者体验为起点的方法。

intro.en: Empathetic is the longer of two adjectives built on empathy, which is itself built from Greek pieces.
intro.cn: empathetic 是建在 empathy 之上的两个形容词中较长的那个，而 empathy 本身由希腊语构件构成。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek, not Latin: en- 'in', pathos 'feeling', and the adjective ending -etikos. No Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这些构件属希腊语而非拉丁语：en-「在内」、pathos「感受」，以及形容词词尾 -etikos。因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The prefix puts the feeling inside the other person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把感受放进他人之内。

items.example: The root supplies the emotional core.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供情感核心。

items.example: The Greek noun stands behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的来源。

items.example: The older adjective survives in clinical writing.
items.exampleCN: 较旧的形容词仍用于临床写作。

items.example: Her reply was brief and empathetic.
items.exampleCN: 她的回答简短而体察人心。

items.example: She tried to empathize with the caller.

items.exampleCN: 他是个有耐心的共情者。

definition_zh: 共犯；帮凶；同伙
definition_en: a person who helps another person commit a crime
core_image: 一个人动手，另一个人在门口望风
scene: 监控里看到，进店偷东西的只有一人，但门外有人不断打手势提醒时间。 Police later arrested his accomplice.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplice 是「共犯、帮凶」（第 1 个义项：协助他人犯罪者）；句意为警方后来逮捕了他的同伙。

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「陪同」，语义上指同行之人
形近但不同源，义为「完成」

senses.title: A helper in a crime
senses.definition: a person who knowingly helps another to commit an offence
senses.definitionCN: 明知而协助他人实施犯罪的人
senses.example: The driver was charged as an accomplice in the escape.
senses.exampleCN: 司机作为逃跑帮凶被起诉。
senses.why: The word grew from complice, 'one joined with another'; in law that joining is a partnership in wrongdoing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 complice（与他人联结者）演变而来；法律上这种联结就是共同作恶的伙伴关系。

senses.title: A partner in mischief
senses.definition: a person who joins another in a mischievous or foolish act, without legal seriousness
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起做淘气或愚蠢之事者，不含法律严重性
senses.example: Her little brother was her accomplice in hiding the cake.
senses.exampleCN: 她弟弟是她藏蛋糕的同伙。
senses.why: Outside law, the word's 'partner' frame survives in jokes: the partner shares the scheme, if not the crime.
senses.whyCN: 在法律之外，这个词的「伙伴」框架残存在玩笑中：伙伴分担的是主意，未必是罪。

intro.en: Accomplice comes from Old French complice, reshaped by association with accomplish; both trace to Latin complere, 'to fill up'.
intro.cn: accomplice 来自古法语 complice，因与 accomplish 联想而被改写；二者都可追到拉丁语 complere（填满）。

items.en: complere meant 'to fill up, complete', from com- and plere 'to fill'.
items.cn: complere 意为「填满、完成」，由 com- 与 plere（填）构成。

items.en: complex meant 'woven together, closely connected'.
items.cn: complex 意为「交织在一起、紧密关联的」。

items.en: complice meant an associate or partner in a matter.
items.cn: complice 指某事中的同伙或伙伴。

items.en: English borrowed complice, then inserted an a by confusion with accomplish.
items.cn: 英语借入 complice，后因与 accomplish 混淆而插入 a。

items.en: Criminal law fixed accomplice for a person who aids an offence.
items.cn: 刑法固定 accomplice 指协助犯罪者。

items.en: Modern usage keeps the legal sense and a lighter playful one.
items.cn: 现代用法保留法律义与较轻的戏谑义。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alikes often confused with it; the second gathers words for a partner in wrongdoing.
note.cn: 第一组收易混的近形词；第二组收表示共同作恶者的词。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to complete a task successfully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「完成、实现」。

entries.definition: An adjective for a highly skilled person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「技艺高超的」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to go with someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「陪同」，与 accomplice 非同源。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning obedient to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「顺从的、合规的」。

entries.definition: A general word for a person working with another.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伙伴」，泛指与他人合作者。

entries.definition: A legal term for a person who assists a crime.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，法律用语，义为「从犯」。

entries.definition: A person joined with others in a plot.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同谋者」，参与密谋者。

entries.definition: A loyal follower who carries out another's plans.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「亲信、打手」，执行他人计划者。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the inserted-a story and the police phrases; the abstract hooks picture one thief inside and one watcher outside.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「插入 a」的拼写故事与警务搭配；抽象记忆点想象一人店内行窃、一人在外望风。

normal.en: Accomplice looks like accomplish, but it means a partner in crime.
normal.cn: accomplice 看起来像 accomplish，却指犯罪同伙。

normal.en: The a was inserted by confusion with accomplish.
normal.cn: 那个 a 是因与 accomplish 混淆而插入的。

normal.en: An accomplice to the crime is the standard legal phrase.
normal.cn: an accomplice to the crime 是标准法律短语。

normal.en: The plural is accomplices, keeping the c soft.
normal.cn: 复数是 accomplices，c 仍读软音。

normal.en: In law, accomplice and accessory are distinct roles.
normal.cn: 法律上 accomplice 与 accessory 是不同角色。

abstract.en: Picture one person inside a shop and one watching the street.
abstract.cn: 想象一人在店内、一人在街上望风。

abstract.en: Picture two children hiding a cake in a cupboard.
abstract.cn: 想象两个孩子把蛋糕藏进橱柜。

abstract.en: Picture a driver waiting with the engine running.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车开着引擎等待。

examples.en: She was convicted as an accomplice in the fraud.
examples.cn: 她作为诈骗案共犯被定罪。

examples.en: The robber's accomplice waited in the car.
examples.cn: 劫匪的同伙在车里等候。

examples.en: His accomplice in the prank was the quietest boy in class.
examples.cn: 他搞恶作剧的同伙是班上最安静的男孩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利斯」——一个人动手，另一个人在门口打手势，就是帮凶。

root: 拉丁语 com-（一起）+ plere（填）→ complex（交织）→ 古法语 complice；核心义是「与他人绑在同一件事上的人」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the legal partner in a crime, to the lighter partner in mischief.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从法律上的犯罪同伙，走到较轻的恶作剧同伙。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person acts while another stands watch
core.cn: 核心意象：一人行动，另一人望风

branches.en: A person who knowingly aids an offence.
branches.cn: 明知而协助犯罪者。

branches.en: A partner in a harmless prank.
branches.cn: 无害恶作剧中的伙伴。

branches.en: Both senses rest on a shared scheme.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在共同的谋划上。

branches.en: The legal word and the playful word are one frame with different weights.
branches.cn: 法律词与戏谑词是同一框架的不同分量。

branches.en: A partner's role ranges from watching to sharing the blame.
branches.cn: 伙伴的角色从望风到分担罪责。

intro.en: The word keeps a Latin 'together' prefix and a filling root, with the -ice ending marking a person.
intro.cn: 这个词保留拉丁语「一起」前缀与「填」词根，并以 -ice 后缀指人。

latinIntro.en: Latin complex and the French form complice are the ancestors, so the Latin entries record the root and the derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 complex 与法语形式 complice 是祖先，因此拉丁条目记录词根与派生形容词。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「陪同」（同源，指同行之人）

definition_zh: 恶化；加重；恼怒；烦躁
definition_en: the act of making something worse; a feeling of annoyance
core_image: 压在伤腿上的另一块石头：本已不堪，还要加码
scene: 雨越下越大，屋顶的漏洞让霉斑迅速蔓延。 The aggravation of the damp problem forced the family to move out.
sceneCN: 这里 aggravation 是「恶化、加重」（第 1 个义项：状况变得更糟）；句意是潮湿问题不断恶化，一家人不得不搬走。

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「使恶化；激怒」
aggravate 加 -ing，义为「令人恼火的；使加重的」
aggravate 加 -ed，义为「恶化的；（罪行）加重的」
同根形容词，义为「严重的；沉重的」

senses.title: The act of making a condition worse
senses.definition: the process of increasing the seriousness of an illness, problem, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、问题或局势的严重程度上升的过程
senses.example: The aggravation of the damp problem forced the family to move out.
senses.exampleCN: 潮湿问题不断恶化，一家人不得不搬走。
senses.why: The Latin root gravis means heavy; aggravation is literally adding weight to what already presses down.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 gravis 意为「重」；aggravation 的本义就是往已经很沉的东西上再加砝码。

senses.title: A feeling of annoyance or exasperation
senses.definition: a state of being irritated, especially by repeated small troubles
senses.definitionCN: 被激怒的状态，尤指被反复的小麻烦磨出来的火气
senses.example: Every phone call with the insurer is pure aggravation.
senses.exampleCN: 每次和保险公司通电话都是纯粹的煎熬。
senses.why: In American colloquial speech, adding weight to the mind became adding irritation, so the emotional sense split off.
senses.whyCN: 美式口语把「给心灵加压」转成「添堵」，于是从「加重」义分岔出「恼怒、烦躁」的情绪义。

intro.en: From Latin aggravatio, built on gravis (heavy); the legal sense of worsening an offence came first, the emotional sense much later.
intro.cn: 源自拉丁语 aggravatio，建立在 gravis（重）之上；先有「罪行加重」的法律义，「恼怒」的口语义出现很晚。

items.en: The root *gwere- (heavy) underlies gravis, grave, and grief.
items.cn: 重构词根 *gwere-（重）是 gravis、grave 与 grief 的共同远源。

items.en: gravis meant heavy; aggravare meant to make heavier.
items.cn: 拉丁语 gravis 意为「重的」，aggravare 意为「使更重」。

items.en: aggravatio named the heightening of a charge's seriousness in Roman law.
items.cn: 法律拉丁语中 aggravatio 指加重罪行的严重程度。

items.en: Borrowed for the worsening of diseases and offences; aggravated burglary survives in law.
items.cn: 借入英语后用于病情与罪行的加重；aggravated burglary 至今仍是法律用语。

items.en: Colloquial American use shifted the word to mean provocation and annoyance.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪美式口语转向「挑衅、惹恼」，情绪义由此确立。

note.en: Aggravation spans the heavy family of grave and grief; annoyance names the feeling without the added weight.
note.cn: aggravation 连着 grave、grief 的「沉重」词族；annoyance 只指情绪，不含「雪上加霜」之意。

entries.definition: the easing of pain or trouble

normal.en: aggravation = aggravate + -ion: the worsening itself
normal.cn: aggravation ＝ aggravate（恶化）+ -ion（名词），即「恶化」本身

normal.en: grave, gravity, grief, aggravation: the heavy family
normal.cn: grave、gravity、grief、aggravation 同属「沉重」家族

normal.en: aggravated assault: legal term with aggravation built in
normal.cn: aggravated assault（加重攻击罪）是法律中的 aggravation

normal.en: pure aggravation: colloquial for a total annoyance
normal.cn: pure aggravation 是口语说法：纯粹的烦人精

normal.en: aggravate versus irritate: add weight versus rub raw
normal.cn: aggravate 是「加码」，irritate 是「磨破」，情绪轻重有别

abstract.en: A second stone stacked on an already sinking boat
abstract.cn: 船上已经吃水极深，还有人往上再压一块石头

abstract.en: A leak in the roof growing wider with every rain
abstract.cn: 屋顶的裂缝逢雨必宽，霉斑一寸寸蔓延

abstract.en: A phone tree that loops forever while the coffee goes cold
abstract.cn: 语音电话无限转接，咖啡凉透还没找到真人

examples.en: Stress is known to cause aggravation of skin conditions.
examples.cn: 众所周知，压力会使皮肤病加重。

examples.en: He endured the daily aggravations of a two-hour commute without complaint.
examples.cn: 他毫无怨言地忍受着每天两小时通勤的种种煎熬。

examples.en: The report warned of the aggravation of drought across the region.
examples.cn: 报告警告该地区的旱情将进一步加剧。

sensesIntro.cn: 「加码」的一个意象分出两支：客观状况的恶化，与主观耐性的耗损。

branches.en: illness or problems growing more serious

branches.en: pressure that keeps mounting
branches.cn: 不断累积的压力

branches.cn: 被小麻烦磨掉的耐性

latinIntro.cn: grav 词根家族贯穿法律、物理与情感词汇。

definition_en: the movement of heat, electricity, sound or nerve signals through a material without the material itself moving
core_image: 一根金属棒的一端浸在热水里，另一端很快也变得烫手，热沿着棒身一路走过去
scene: 物理课上，学生把金属棒的一端放进热水，很快握住另一端的手也感到烫，老师说 Heat moves along the rod by conduction.
sceneCN: 这里 conduction 指「热在物质内部逐层传递、物质本身并不整体移动」（第 1 个义项：固体中的热传导）；句意为热沿着金属棒传导过来。图中可辨识物件：金属棒、热水杯、温度计、握住棒端的手。
