senses.title: Heat moving through a solid
senses.definition: the transfer of heat through a material by the vibration of particles, without the material moving as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 热通过粒子的振动在材料内部传递，而材料整体并不移动
senses.example: Copper is used in cookware because its heat conduction is fast.
senses.exampleCN: 铜被用于炊具，因为它的热传导很快。
senses.why: Latin conducere 'to lead along' gives the image of heat being led through the body of a material.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 conducere「沿着引导」给出一个意象：热被引导着穿过材料本身。

senses.title: Electric current through a material
senses.definition: the flow of electric charge through a substance when a voltage is applied
senses.definitionCN: 施加电压时电荷在物质中的流动
senses.example: The salt solution supports electrical conduction.
senses.exampleCN: 盐溶液可以导电。
senses.why: Electricity was understood as a flow that is 'led' through a wire, so the same noun was reused.
senses.whyCN: 电被理解为一种被「引导」通过导线的流动，于是沿用了同一个名词。

senses.title: Ionic conduction in solutions
senses.definition: charge transport by ions moving through a liquid or a solid electrolyte
senses.definitionCN: 离子在液体或固体电解质中移动而完成的电荷输运
senses.example: Ionic conduction in the battery depends on how freely the ions move.
senses.exampleCN: 电池中的离子传导取决于离子移动的自由程度。
senses.why: Here the carriers are whole ions rather than electrons, but the leading-through image is unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这里的载体是整个离子而非电子，但「引导穿过」的意象没有改变。

senses.title: Nerve signal conduction
senses.definition: the passage of an electrical impulse along a nerve fibre
senses.definitionCN: 电冲动沿神经纤维的传递
senses.example: Damage to the sheath slows nerve conduction.
senses.exampleCN: 髓鞘受损会减慢神经传导。
senses.why: Physiology borrowed the physics word because a signal also travels along a pathway without the pathway moving.
senses.whyCN: 生理学借用了物理词，因为信号同样沿路径行进，而路径本身不动。

senses.title: Sound conduction
senses.definition: the passing of sound vibrations through a solid, liquid or gas, especially through the ear
senses.definitionCN: 声音振动通过固体、液体或气体传递，尤指经过耳部
senses.example: Bone conduction lets you hear a vibration through your skull.
senses.exampleCN: 骨传导让你能通过颅骨听到振动。
senses.why: Vibration travelling through matter is another case of something being led along a medium.
senses.whyCN: 振动穿过物质，同样是某物被沿着介质引导而行的情形。

senses.title: Leading or guidance
senses.definition: the act of leading, guiding or managing something, the earliest sense of the word in English
senses.definitionCN: 引导、指导或管理某事的动作，这是该词进入英语时最早的意思
senses.example: The old text speaks of the conduction of a household.
senses.exampleCN: 这份旧文献谈到对一个家庭的治理。
senses.why: The modern scientific senses all grow from this plain sense of leading: heat, charge and signals are all led along.
senses.whyCN: 现代科学义都从「引导」这一朴素义生长出来：热、电荷与信号都是被引导着走的。

senses.title: Heat loss through a building
senses.titleCN: 建筑围护结构的热传导
senses.definition: the rate at which heat passes through walls, windows and roofs into or out of a building
senses.definitionCN: 热穿过墙体、窗户与屋顶进出建筑的速率
senses.example: Double glazing reduces conduction through the window.
senses.exampleCN: 双层玻璃减少了通过窗户的热传导。
senses.why: Building science applies the solid-state process to the fabric of a house.
senses.whyCN: 建筑科学把固体传热过程套用到房屋的围护结构上。

senses.title: Conduction in semiconductors
senses.definition: charge transport by electrons and holes in a material whose conductivity lies between a metal and an insulator
senses.definitionCN: 在导电性介于金属与绝缘体之间的材料中，由电子与空穴完成的电荷输运
senses.example: Doping raises the conduction of silicon at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 掺杂提高了硅在室温下的导电能力。
senses.why: The band model describes two kinds of carrier, but both are still conducted through the lattice.
senses.whyCN: 能带模型描述了两种载流子，但两者都仍是穿过晶格被传导的。

intro.en: Conduction comes from Latin conducere 'to lead or bring together', built on com- 'together' and ducere 'to lead'. The word entered English first as 'guidance' and only later became a term for heat, charge and nerve signals.
intro.cn: conduction 来自拉丁 conducere「引导、聚拢」，由 com-「一起」与 ducere「引导」构成。它进入英语时先表示「引导」，后来才成为热、电荷与神经信号方面的术语。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead, draw, guide', with the past participle ductus; it also gives duct, duke and induce.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导、拉、带领」，过去分词为 ductus；它还给出 duct、duke 与 induce。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus ducere produced conducere 'to lead together, bring along, hire'.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 ducere 构成 conducere「引导到一起、带来、雇用」。

items.en: The action noun conductio 'a leading, hiring' supplied the form that English borrowed.
items.cn: 动作名词 conductio「引导、雇用」提供了英语借入的形式。

items.en: In Middle English conduction meant leading or guidance; the scientific senses are much later additions.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，conduction 意为引导或管理；科学义是后来才加上的。

items.en: The heat and electricity senses date from the nineteenth century; the exact first use in each field is uncertain.
items.cn: 热与电的义项始于 19 世纪；各领域确切的最早使用不确定。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same Latin root that are easily confused; group two holds the other heat-transfer modes and related transport words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、容易混淆的形式；第二组是其他传热方式与相关的输运词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to lead, carry out or transmit, and the noun for a person's behaviour; conduction is only the process noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词意为引导、进行或传输，名词指人的行为；conduction 只是表示过程的名词。

entries.definition: A material or person that conducts heat, electricity, sound or an orchestra; it names the agent, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 传导热、电、声的材料，或指挥乐队的人；它指施动者而非过程。

entries.definition: The degree to which a material conducts heat or electricity, a quantity rather than the flow itself.
entries.definitionCN: 材料传导热或电的程度，是一个量，而不是流动本身。

entries.definition: A pipe or channel through which something passes, from the same root but naming the physical channel.
entries.definitionCN: 让某物通过的管道或通道，同出该词根，但指实物通道。

entries.definition: Heat transfer by a moving fluid; in conduction the material stays put while energy passes through it.
entries.definitionCN: 由流动的流体传热；传导中材料本身不动，能量穿过它。

entries.definition: Heat transfer by electromagnetic waves, needing no material medium at all.
entries.definitionCN: 以电磁波传热，完全不需要物质介质。

entries.definition: The general passing of energy, signals or disease from one place to another, without specifying the mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 能量、信号或疾病从一处传到另一处的泛称，不指明机制。

entries.definition: The spreading of particles from high to low concentration; it moves matter itself rather than leading energy through a fixed lattice.
entries.definitionCN: 粒子由高浓度向低浓度散开；它移动的是物质本身，而非让能量穿过固定晶格。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real word family and real physics collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实词族与真实物理搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' + ducere 'lead': energy is led through the material.
normal.cn: con-「一起」+ ducere「引导」：能量被引导穿过材料。

normal.en: The root family runs conduct, conductor, conductivity, conduit.
normal.cn: 词根词族包括 conduct、conductor、conductivity、conduit。

normal.en: Physics pairs it with convection and radiation as the three modes of heat transfer.
normal.cn: 物理学把它与 convection、radiation 并列为三种传热方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: heat conduction, electrical conduction, conduction band.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：热传导、导电、导带。

normal.en: The oldest sense is guidance; every later sense keeps the idea of something being led along.
normal.cn: 最古老的义项是引导；后来每个义项都保留「某物被引导着前行」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a line of people passing buckets along until the last one gets water.
abstract.cn: 想象一排人依次传递水桶，直到最后一个人接到水。

abstract.en: Picture a whisper travelling down a row of seated students without anyone moving seats.
abstract.cn: 想象一句耳语沿一排坐着的学生传下去，没有人换座位。

abstract.en: Picture a copper spoon in a hot pot, its handle warming long before it is touched.
abstract.cn: 想象热锅里的铜勺，还没碰到，勺柄就已经暖了。

examples.en: Silver has excellent conduction, which is why it is used in some contacts.
examples.cn: 银的导电性极好，因此被用于某些触点。

examples.en: Thick insulation slows conduction through the walls.
examples.cn: 厚保温层减缓了通过墙体的热传导。

examples.en: The doctor ordered a test of nerve conduction in the arm.
examples.cn: 医生安排了手臂神经传导的检查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯导」——热肯沿着棒子一路导过去，就是传导

root: 拉丁 conducere「引导、聚拢」= com-「一起」+ ducere「引导」，动作名词 conductio。英语先有「引导、管理」义，热、电、神经等科学义始于 19 世纪；各领域最早书证不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: something is led through a medium that itself stays still, whether that something is heat, charge, an ion, a nerve impulse, sound, or the older idea of guidance itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：某物被引导穿过本身不动的介质，无论那是热、电荷、离子、神经冲动、声音，还是更早的「引导」这一本义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heat walking along a metal rod while the rod stays where it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：热沿着金属棒走过去，而棒子本身停在原处。

branches.en: HEAT IN MATTER: the same process is measured in a rod and in a house wall.
branches.cn: 物质中的热：同一过程既在金属棒上测量，也在房屋墙体上测量。

branches.en: CHARGE CARRIERS: electrons and ions both conduct, though the carriers differ.
branches.cn: 电荷载体：电子与离子都能传导，只是载体不同。

branches.en: LIVING AND VIBRATING SIGNALS: nerves and sound repeat the same leading-through pattern.
branches.cn: 生命与振动信号：神经与声音重复同样的引导模式。

branches.en: THE ORIGINAL SENSE: guidance is the plain meaning from which the science grew.
branches.cn: 本义：引导是科学义生长出来的朴素含义。

branches.en: SEMICONDUCTORS: two kinds of carrier share one lattice.
branches.cn: 半导体：两种载流子共用一套晶格。

intro.en: Conduction is con- plus the root duc- plus -tion; the same three pieces build a large and very common family.
intro.cn: conduction 是 con- 加词根 duc- 再加 -tion；同样三块构成一个庞大而常见的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is well recorded: ducere 'to lead', conducere 'to lead together', conductio 'a leading', and the participle ductus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族记载完整：ducere「引导」、conducere「引导到一起」、conductio「引导」以及分词 ductus。

items.example: The prefix gathers the leading into one movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把引导收束为一次整体运动。

items.example: The root also appears in induce and duct.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也出现在 induce 与 duct 中。

items.meaning: the act or result of an action
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程之名。

items.meaning: to lead, carry out or transmit

items.structure: conduct + -or (one who or that which acts)
items.meaning: a material that transmits heat or electricity
items.example: A conductor carries charge to the ground.

items.meaning: able to conduct heat or electricity
items.example: The gel is conductive and harmless to skin.
items.exampleCN: 这种凝胶导电且对皮肤无害。

items.example: Copper's conductivity is higher than iron's.

items.meaning: a pipe or channel for passing something
items.meaningCN: 输送某物的管道或通道
items.example: Water ran through the stone conduit.

items.meaning: the ease with which a component conducts
items.example: The circuit's conductance fell as it warmed.
items.exampleCN: 电路升温时其电导下降。

latinEntries.meaning: to lead together, bring along, hire

definition_zh: 自我意识；对自身情绪、状态与形象的认识
definition_en: knowledge of one's own feelings, character, body or effect on other people
core_image: 一个人站在镜前，不只看见脸，还看见自己刚才为什么皱眉
scene: 练功房里，舞者反复看自己排练的录像，留意重心如何移动。 The video gives her a sharper self-awareness of how she shifts her weight.
sceneCN: 这里 self-awareness 指「对自身动作状态的清楚认识」（第 1 个义项：对自身状态的认识）；句意为录像让她更清楚地意识到自己怎样转移重心。场景要素：排练录像、地胶、镜子、水杯。

pos.zh: 自我意识；对自身状态与形象的认识

collocations.zh: 对他人眼中形象的意识

derivatives.zh: 由 self-awareness 去掉名词后缀构成的形容词，指对自身有认识的
该复合词的中心词，指对某事的察觉状态
由否定前缀加 aware 构成，指未察觉的
另一条复合词，指过度在意他人目光的，与自我认识不是同一件事
另一条复合词，指对自身性格的深层了解，偏静态而非当下觉察

senses.title: Knowledge of one's own feelings and character
senses.titleCN: 对自身情绪与性格的认识
senses.definition: a clear sense of what one feels, wants and is like as a person
senses.definitionCN: 对自身感受、愿望以及自己是怎样一个人的清楚认识
senses.example: Years of journaling gave him a quiet self-awareness about his temper.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的日记让他对自己的脾气有了一种沉静的自觉。
senses.why: The compound joins the pronoun for one's own person to the word for being alert, so its first sense is simply being alert to oneself.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把指「自身」的代词接到表示「警觉」的词上，因此第一个义项就是对自己保持警觉。

senses.title: Awareness of how others see you
senses.titleCN: 意识到他人如何看待自己
senses.definition: recognition of the impression one makes on other people, including the unintended one
senses.definitionCN: 认识到自己给他人留下的印象，包括那些并非本意的印象
senses.example: The feedback session raised her self-awareness about how often she interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 反馈环节让她意识到自己打断别人的次数有多频繁。
senses.why: Once the gaze turns outward and then back, a person can see the version of herself that exists in other minds.
senses.whyCN: 当目光先向外再折回，人就能看见存在于他人心中的那个自己。

senses.title: Awareness of one's body and posture
senses.definition: noticing where one's body is, how it is balanced and what it is doing
senses.definitionCN: 留意身体的位置、平衡方式与正在做的动作
senses.example: Ballet training builds self-awareness of the angle of the pelvis.
senses.exampleCN: 芭蕾训练培养对骨盆角度的身体自觉。
senses.why: Proprioception is the oldest layer of the compound: the body reporting on itself before language does.
senses.whyCN: 本体感觉是这个复合词最古老的一层：身体先于语言向自己报告。

senses.title: Knowing one's limits and biases
senses.titleCN: 知道自己的局限与偏见
senses.definition: an accurate sense of where one's knowledge stops and where one's judgment is skewed
senses.definitionCN: 对自己知识止于何处、判断偏向何处有准确的感觉
senses.example: Good forecasters show self-awareness about the topics they overrate.
senses.exampleCN: 优秀的预测者对自己高估的领域有清醒的自觉。
senses.why: Knowing one's edges is the practical payoff of self-awareness, because a limit that is seen can be planned around.
senses.whyCN: 知道自己的边界是自我意识的实用回报，因为被看见的局限可以被绕开。

senses.title: Monitoring oneself in the moment
senses.definition: catching oneself in the middle of an action and adjusting before it finishes
senses.definitionCN: 在行动进行中察觉自己，并在结束前作出调整
senses.example: Halfway through the argument she noticed her voice rising and stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 争到一半，她察觉自己声音在升高，于是停了下来。
senses.why: The same awareness can run live rather than retrospectively, and this live version is what allows correction in real time.
senses.whyCN: 同一种觉察可以不事后而是实时运行，正是这种实时版本让人能够即时修正。

senses.title: Philosophical self-consciousness
senses.titleCN: 哲学意义上的自我意识
senses.definition: the condition of a subject that is aware of itself as the one experiencing
senses.definitionCN: 主体意识到自己正是那个正在体验的人这一状态
senses.example: The seminar asked whether self-awareness can exist without language.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课追问：没有语言是否还能有自我意识。
senses.why: Philosophy pushed the everyday sense to its limit, asking what it means for a mind to be an object to itself.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常义推到极限，追问一颗心智把自己当作对象究竟意味着什么。

senses.title: A system representing its own state
senses.titleCN: 系统对自身状态的表征
senses.definition: in technical use, the capacity of a system to hold a model of its own condition or reliability
senses.definitionCN: 在技术语境中，指系统持有关于自身状况或可靠性的模型
senses.example: The monitoring module gives the robot a crude self-awareness of its battery and balance.
senses.exampleCN: 监控模块让机器人对自己的电量和平衡有了粗略的自我感知。
senses.why: Engineers reuse the everyday term for machines that must report on themselves, and the borrowing is openly approximate.
senses.whyCN: 工程师把日常说法挪用到必须报告自身状态的机器上，这种借用是公开的近似。

senses.title: Reflective awareness of one's learning
senses.titleCN: 对自身学习的反思性觉察
senses.definition: noticing how one studies, what one avoids and which habits help
senses.definitionCN: 留意自己如何学习、回避什么、哪些习惯有用
senses.example: The portfolio asks students for self-awareness about their own revision habits.
senses.exampleCN: 这份学习档案要求学生反思自己的复习习惯。
senses.why: In education the compound narrows to learning, where awareness of habits is the first step to changing them.
senses.whyCN: 在教育语境中，这个复合词收窄到学习上：对习惯的觉察是改变习惯的第一步。

intro.en: Self-awareness joins an Old English pronoun for one's own person to an English word for being watchful, and the compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: self-awareness 把古英语中指「自身」的代词，接到英语中表「警觉」的词上；这个复合词是近现代产物。年代均为约数。

items.en: Self worked as a pronoun and an adjective meaning 'the same person'. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: self 兼作代词与形容词，意为「同一个人」。其更早来源未得到证明。

items.en: Gewær meant 'watchful, wary', from a root for guarding; the modern word aware appears in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: gewær 意为「警觉的、留心的」，出自表「看守」的词根；现代词形在十六世纪出现。

items.en: The compound self-awareness was built in the nineteenth century, first in philosophy and early psychology.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十九世纪构成，最早出现在哲学与早期心理学中。

items.en: Twentieth-century psychology separated private awareness of one's inner state from public awareness of how one is seen.
items.cn: 二十世纪心理学把对内在状态的私下觉察，与对「自己如何被看见」的公开觉察区分开来。

items.en: Late twentieth-century engineering added the technical sense of a system that models its own condition.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期，工程学增添了技术义：系统对自身状况建立模型。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation and deeper origin): the exact first printed use of the compound is unsettled, and the pre-Old-English origin of self is unknown, so any earlier form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（最早书证与更深来源）：这个复合词的确切最早用例尚无定论；self 在古英语之前的来源亦不可考，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same self- or awareness stock that are constantly confused; group two holds near neighbours that name knowledge of oneself in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「自身」或「觉察」词干、极易混淆的词；第二组是以别的方式指「认识自己」的近义词。

entries.definition: Means awkwardly aware of being watched; the awareness is turned up until it interferes, which is not implied by self-awareness.
entries.definitionCN: 指因被他人注视而局促，觉察强到妨碍行动，这层意思 self-awareness 并不带。

entries.definition: The noun matching the uneasy adjective, and also a philosophical term for a subject aware of itself.
entries.definitionCN: 是与那个局促形容词对应的名词，也作哲学术语指自我意识到自身的主体。

entries.definition: Alertness to anything at all, from traffic to a rumour; it lacks the inward direction of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指对任何事物的警觉，从车流到传闻；缺少这个复合词的向内方向。

entries.definition: The general state of being awake and sentient, far broader than knowing one's own character.
entries.definitionCN: 指清醒而有感觉的一般状态，比「了解自己性格」宽泛得多。

entries.definition: The deliberate examination of one's own thoughts; it is a method, while self-awareness is the resulting knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意审视自身念头，是一种方法；自我意识是这样做之后得到的知识。

entries.definition: A lasting understanding of one's character, gained over years; self-awareness can also be a sharp momentary state.
entries.definitionCN: 指多年积累的、对自身性格的持久了解；自我意识也可以是当下的一瞬清醒。

entries.definition: A trained attention to the present moment; self-awareness may be anxious, evaluative or purely practical.
entries.definitionCN: 指训练有素地注意当下；自我意识则可能是焦虑的、评判性的或纯实用的。

entries.definition: Thinking over an experience afterwards; self-awareness includes instant awareness with no thinking back at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指事后对某段经历的思考；自我意识也包含完全不必回想的即时觉察。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves of the compound and the real phrases it forms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：这个复合词两个真实的构成部分，以及它构成的真实短语。

normal.en: The first half means one's own person and the second means being alert, so together they read 'alert to oneself'.
normal.cn: 前半指「自身」，后半指「警觉」，合起来就是「对自己保持警觉」。

normal.en: The adjective is self-aware and the bare noun is awareness, a family of three forms.
normal.cn: 形容词是 self-aware，去掉自身成分的名词是 awareness，共三种词形。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: develop self-awareness, heightened self-awareness, emotional self-awareness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出使用范围：培养自我意识、更强的自我意识、情绪上的自我觉察。

normal.en: Psychology separates the private version from the public version, where the second is about being seen.
normal.cn: 心理学把私下觉察与公开觉察分开，后者关乎「被看见」。

normal.en: Engineering borrows the word for machines that must report their own battery or balance.
normal.cn: 工程学把这个词借去指必须报告自身电量或平衡的机器。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror that shows not only the face but the reason for the frown.
abstract.cn: 想象一面不只照出脸、还照出皱眉原因的镜子。

abstract.en: Picture a torch that the walker points at her own feet.
abstract.cn: 想象走路的人把手电照向自己的脚。

abstract.en: Picture a report card a machine writes about its own condition.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器给自己写出一份状况报告。

examples.en: The training aims to give new managers self-awareness about how they speak under pressure.
examples.cn: 这项培训旨在让新经理意识到自己在压力下说话的样子。

examples.en: Her self-awareness of the gap between her plan and her practice was unusually exact.
examples.cn: 她对自己计划与实践之间差距的自觉异常精确。

examples.en: A little self-awareness would have prevented the remark.
examples.cn: 只要有一点自我觉察，那句话就不会说出口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「self 自己 + awareness 觉察」——对自己保持觉察，就是自我意识

root: 古英语 self「自身」+ 英语 aware「警觉的」及其名词后缀；aware 出自意为「看守」的古英语词根，self 的更早来源不确定。英语 self-awareness。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: attention turned back on the person who is attending. It covers feelings and character, the image others hold, the body, the edges of one's knowledge, live self-correction, philosophical selfhood, a machine's self-report and the study of one's own habits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：注意力折回到正在注意的人身上。它覆盖情绪与性格、他人心中的形象、身体、知识的边界、实时的自我修正、哲学上的自我、机器的自我报告，以及对自身习惯的审视。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone at a mirror who sees not only the face but the reason for the frown.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在镜前的人不只看见脸，还看见自己皱眉的原因。

branches.en: INNER AND LIVE: settled knowledge of one's feelings, and the same knowledge caught in the middle of an action.
branches.cn: 内在与实时：对情绪的稳定认识，以及在行动中途被抓住的同一种认识。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE VIEW: the self that exists in other minds is seen only by turning the gaze outward first.
branches.cn: 外部视角：存在于他人心中的自己，只有先把目光向外才看得见。

branches.en: BODY AND EDGES: posture is the oldest layer, and the limits of knowledge are the most useful one.
branches.cn: 身体与边界：姿态是最古老的一层，知识的边界是最有用的一层。

branches.en: THEORETICAL AND PRACTICAL: philosophy asks what selfhood is, while education asks which study habits one actually has.
branches.cn: 理论与实用：哲学追问自我是什么，教育则追问自己实际有哪些学习习惯。

branches.en: SELF-REPORTING MACHINE: a system that models its own condition borrows the everyday word.
branches.cn: 自我报告的机器：对自身状况建模的系统借用了这个日常词。

intro.en: The compound is English throughout: an Old English pronoun plus an English noun, which is why it splits cleanly into two readable halves.
intro.cn: 这个复合词从头到尾都是英语：一个古英语代词加一个英语名词，因此可以干净地切成两个可读的部分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here; the neighbouring family is English, running self, self-aware, awareness, unaware and self-conscious.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语成分；相邻的词族是英语自身的，包括 self、self-aware、awareness、unaware 与 self-conscious。

items.example: The first half points the whole word back at the person.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分让整个词指回本人。

items.structure: aware (English adjective, from an Old English word for watchful)
items.example: The second half supplies the noticing.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分提供「察觉」的意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective aware into a state that can grow or fade.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成可以增减的状态。

items.example: The bare noun is the centre of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个不带自身成分的名词是复合词的中心。

items.example: The compound aims the bare noun at the person who has it.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把那个名词对准拥有它的本人。

items.example: The adjective drops the state suffix and keeps the quality.
items.exampleCN: 形容词去掉表状态的后缀，只留性质。

items.example: The negative prefix marks the absence of the whole state.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀标出整个状态的缺席。

items.example: A different second half gives a different, uneasy meaning.
items.exampleCN: 换掉后半部分，意思就变成局促不安。

items.example: Another compound shows the same first half with a lasting second half.
items.exampleCN: 另一个复合词用同样的前半，配上表示持久了解的后半。

definition_zh: 修复；补救；整治；对受污染场地或受损系统采取的治疗性措施
definition_en: the act of correcting a harm or repairing a damaged system, especially the cleanup of a contaminated site
core_image: 废弃加油站的地面上，工人铲起被油浸黑的表土，送进一台加热脱附的机器
scene: 废弃的加油站场地上，工人把受油污染的表土铲进热脱附设备。 Remediation of the old fuel site took three years.
sceneCN: 这里 remediation 指「对受污染场地进行清理与整治」（第 2 个义项：把土壤、地下水中的污染物去除或降低到安全水平）；句意为这座旧燃料场地的修复用了三年。图中可辨识物件：废弃加油站、油污表土、铲斗、热脱附设备。

pos.zh: 修复；补救；整治（不可数，复数指多项修复工程）

senses.title: The act of putting a fault right
senses.definition: the general act of correcting a fault, weakness or bad condition in something
senses.definitionCN: 纠正某物中的缺陷、弱点或不良状况的总体行为
senses.example: Remediation of the old fuel site took three years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧燃料场地的修复用了三年。
senses.why: Remediation comes from Latin remedium 'a cure', built on re- 'again' plus mederi 'to heal', so it carries the idea of treating a disorder rather than merely covering it.
senses.whyCN: remediation 出自拉丁 remedium「治疗之物」，由 re-「再」加 mederi「治愈」构成，因此带有「治疗失调」而非「遮盖」的意思。

senses.title: Cleanup of a contaminated site
senses.titleCN: 受污染场地的清理整治
senses.definition: the removal, containment or destruction of pollutants in soil, water or buildings so that the site can be used safely
senses.definitionCN: 去除、封存或销毁土壤、水体或建筑中的污染物，使场地可安全使用
senses.example: The state ordered remediation of every closed landfill.
senses.exampleCN: 该州下令对每一座关闭的填埋场进行修复。
senses.why: Environmental law gave the word its dominant modern sense, because a site that has been harmed must be brought back to a usable state.
senses.whyCN: 环境法赋予这个词最主要的现代义，因为受损的场地必须被恢复到可使用状态。

senses.title: Soil remediation
senses.definition: physical, chemical or biological treatment that lowers soil contamination to an accepted level
senses.definitionCN: 把土壤污染降到公认水平的物理、化学或生物处理
senses.example: Thermal treatment was chosen for the soil remediation.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤修复选用了热处理。
senses.why: Soil is the medium that holds contaminants longest, so its treatment is the most visible form of remediation work.
senses.whyCN: 土壤是留住污染物最久的介质，因此它的处理是修复工程中最可见的形式。

senses.title: Groundwater remediation
senses.definition: pumping, treating or chemically converting polluted groundwater until it meets a standard
senses.definitionCN: 把受污染的地下水抽出、处理或用化学方法转化，直到达标
senses.example: Pump-and-treat groundwater remediation ran for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 抽出—处理式的地下水修复持续了十年。
senses.why: Groundwater moves and spreads, so its remediation is slow and is usually described by the method used.
senses.whyCN: 地下水会流动扩散，因此其修复缓慢，通常以所用方法命名。

senses.title: Ecological restoration of a damaged habitat
senses.titleCN: 受损栖息地的生态修复
senses.definition: work that rebuilds the structure, species and processes of a habitat rather than only removing a pollutant
senses.definitionCN: 重建栖息地的结构、物种与过程，而不只是去除某种污染物
senses.example: Wetland remediation brought the reed beds back.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地修复让芦苇荡重新长回来。
senses.why: Remediation can aim at function rather than purity: a habitat is treated until it works again.
senses.whyCN: 修复的目标可以是功能而非纯净：栖息地被整治到能重新运转。

senses.title: Remedial teaching in education
senses.titleCN: 教育中的补习与补救教学
senses.definition: extra instruction given to students who have fallen behind in a subject
senses.definitionCN: 为在某一科目上落后的学生提供的额外教学
senses.example: The school added reading remediation for the lower grades.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为低年级增加了阅读补习。
senses.why: Education uses the same medical shape: a weakness is diagnosed and treated with targeted practice.
senses.whyCN: 教育使用同样的医学形态：先诊断弱点，再用有针对性的练习治疗。

senses.title: Legal remedy and redress
senses.definition: a legal means of putting right a wrong, such as compensation or an order to correct a defect
senses.definitionCN: 纠正过错的法律手段，如赔偿或责令改正
senses.example: The contract gave the buyer remediation for the faulty roof.
senses.exampleCN: 合同赋予买方对缺陷屋顶的补救权。
senses.why: Law borrowed the cure word because a right without a remedy is only a statement.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用「治疗」一词，因为没有救济的权利只是一句声明。

senses.title: Security and software remediation
senses.titleCN: 信息安全与软件的修复
senses.definition: the patching or reconfiguration of a system to close a vulnerability or correct a fault
senses.definitionCN: 通过打补丁或重新配置来封堵漏洞、纠正故障
senses.example: The team finished remediation of the exposed server by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在中午前完成了对暴露服务器的修复。
senses.why: Information security adopted the word because a known flaw must be treated before it is exploited.
senses.whyCN: 信息安全采用这个词，因为已知的缺陷必须在被利用之前处理掉。

senses.title: Abstract: making amends for harm done
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：为造成的损害作出补偿
senses.definition: a transferred use for the social or moral work of repairing damage one has caused
senses.definitionCN: 转指为修复自己造成的损害所做的社会或道德工作
senses.example: The company described its scholarship fund as remediation.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把它的奖学金基金称为一种补救。
senses.why: The medical image survives: a harm has been done, and something must be applied until the harmed body is whole again.
senses.whyCN: 医学意象仍然保留：损害已经发生，必须施加某种东西，直到受损的整体重新完整。

intro.en: Remediation is a modern English noun from Latin remedium 'a cure'. The medical image of treating a disorder runs through every sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: remediation 是近代英语名词，出自拉丁 remedium「治疗之物」。治疗失调的医学意象贯穿所有义项。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mederi meant 'to heal, to look after'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the root often proposed for it, with the sense 'take appropriate measures', is a reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: mederi 意为「治愈、照料」。其更深来源不确定；常为它提出的、意为「采取适当措施」的词根是重构，而非有书证的形式。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus mederi produced remedium 'a cure, a remedy', the thing applied so that health returns.
items.cn: re-「再」加 mederi 构成 remedium「治疗之物、补救办法」，即为了恢复健康而施加的东西。

items.en: Old French remedie brought remedy into English in the fourteenth century, first for a medicine and then for any correction of a wrong.
items.cn: 古法语 remedie 在十四世纪把 remedy 带入英语，先指药物，后指对过错的任何纠正。

items.en: The adjective remedial followed in the seventeenth century; the noun remediation was formed later on the same Latin base.
items.cn: 形容词 remedial 随后在十七世纪出现；名词 remediation 后来在同一拉丁词基上构成。

items.en: Late twentieth-century environmental law made site remediation a standard procedure, and this sense now dominates technical use.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的环境法使场地修复成为标准程序，这一义项如今在技术用法中占主导。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of mederi, first date of the noun): the healing root behind mederi is unsettled, and no single earliest citation is fixed for remediation in its environmental sense, so its date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（mederi 的更深来源、该名词的首见年代）：mederi 背后「治愈」的词根无定论，remediation 的环境义也没有公认的最早书证，年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds words that look close to remediation but come from mederi 'to heal' or from medius 'middle'; the two roots are not related. Group two holds other words for undoing harm.
note.cn: 第一组是外形接近 remediation 的词，分别出自 mederi「治愈」或 medius「中间」，两个词根并无亲缘；第二组是其他表示「消除损害」的词。

entries.definition: A cure or correction, from the same remedium; remediation is the process of applying remedies at scale.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗或纠正，同出 remedium；remediation 是大规模施加补救的过程。

entries.definition: Serving to cure or correct, as in remedial teaching; it describes the treatment, not the whole programme.
entries.definitionCN: 用于治疗或纠正的，如补习教学；它描述治疗，而非整套方案。

entries.definition: To act between two sides to settle a dispute, from Latin medius 'middle'; the similarity to remediate is formal only.
entries.definitionCN: 居于两方之间以解决争端，出自拉丁 medius「中间」；与 remediate 的相似只是形式上的。

entries.definition: Assisted negotiation between parties, from medius 'middle'; it settles a dispute rather than repairing damage.
entries.definitionCN: 由第三方协助的谈判，出自 medius「中间」；它解决争端，而非修复损害。

entries.definition: Returning something to a former or better condition; restoration aims at the original state, while remediation aims at safety.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物回到原先或更好的状态；restoration 以求复原状为目标，remediation 以安全为目标。

entries.definition: The everyday term for removing pollution; remediation is its formal and regulatory counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 去除污染的日常说法；remediation 是其正式、监管用语中的对应词。

entries.definition: Making a harm less severe; mitigation reduces the effect, while remediation treats the damaged medium itself.
entries.definitionCN: 使危害减轻；mitigation 减小影响，remediation 则处理受损的介质本身。

entries.definition: Bringing spoiled land into a usable condition, as after mining; it stresses future use rather than removal of a pollutant.
entries.definitionCN: 把废弃土地恢复到可用状态，如采矿之后；它强调未来用途，而非去除污染物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Remediation is re- 'again' plus mederi 'to heal': apply again until the patient is whole.
normal.cn: remediation 是 re-「再」加 mederi「治愈」：一次又一次施加，直到整体复原。

normal.en: The family runs remedy, remedial, remediate, remediable and irremediable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 remedy、remedial、remediate、remediable 与 irremediable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: site remediation, soil remediation, groundwater remediation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：场地修复、土壤修复、地下水修复。

normal.en: Remediate comes from mederi 'heal'; mediate comes from medius 'middle'. They are not relatives.
normal.cn: remediate 出自 mederi「治愈」；mediate 出自 medius「中间」。二者并非同族。

normal.en: The school sense keeps the medical shape: find the weakness, then treat it with practice.
normal.cn: 教育义保留了医学形态：先找出弱点，再用练习治疗。

abstract.en: Picture a wound cleaned and bound until the skin closes again.
abstract.cn: 想象伤口被清洗包扎，直到皮肤重新合上。

abstract.en: Picture a patch sewn over a tear in a sail before the wind finds it.
abstract.cn: 想象在风找到裂口之前，先给帆补上一块。

abstract.en: Picture a debt repaid slowly, not cancelled.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔债被慢慢偿还，而不是被勾销。

examples.en: Remediation costs are often paid by the party that caused the contamination.
examples.cn: 修复费用通常由造成污染的一方支付。

examples.en: Bioremediation uses microbes to break down the oil in the soil.
examples.cn: 生物修复利用微生物分解土壤中的油。

examples.en: The school's remediation programme targets reading and arithmetic.
examples.cn: 该校的补救教学计划针对阅读与算术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ medi（治愈）+ ation」——再治一次，直到恢复 → 修复、补救

root: 拉丁 remedium「治疗之物」= re-（再）+ mederi「治愈、照料」；mederi 的更深来源不确定，常被提出的「采取适当措施」词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cure: a fault is found, its cause is treated, the medium is cleaned, function returns, law requires it, and finally the same image covers teaching, software and amends.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一次治疗展开：先发现缺陷，再处理成因，接着清理介质，功能恢复，法律要求如此，最后同一意象覆盖教学、软件与补偿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: oil-black soil lifted from an old filling station and fed into a heated cleaner.
core.cn: 核心意象：从旧加油站铲起油黑的土，送进加热的净化设备。

branches.en: CURE AND SITE: the general correction and the contaminated site are the same treatment at two scales.
branches.cn: 治疗与场地：总体纠正与受污染场地，是同一治疗在两个尺度上。

branches.en: TWO MEDIA: soil is treated in place or by heating, groundwater by pumping and treating.
branches.cn: 两种介质：土壤就地处理或加热处理，地下水则抽出处理。

branches.en: FUNCTION: restoration aims at a working habitat, not merely a clean sample.
branches.cn: 功能：修复瞄准的是能运转的栖息地，而不只是干净的样本。

branches.en: TREATMENT ELSEWHERE: a weak pupil and a wronged buyer are both given a remedy.
branches.cn: 别处的治疗：落后的学生与受屈的买家，都被给了一剂补救。

branches.en: TRANSFER: a server flaw and a social harm are treated like a wound.
branches.cn: 转移：服务器漏洞与社会损害，都像伤口一样被处理。

intro.en: Remediation is a Latin-derived noun of curing, with a prefix, a healing root and an action suffix; its look-alike mediate belongs to a different root.
intro.cn: remediation 是拉丁来源的「治疗」名词，含前缀、治愈词根与动作后缀；外形相近的 mediate 属于另一个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin mederi gives remedy, remedial, remediate and irremediable; Latin medius 'middle' gives mediate, mediation, medium and immediate, which are not relatives of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mederi 衍生 remedy、remedial、remediate 与 irremediable；拉丁 medius「中间」衍生 mediate、mediation、medium 与 immediate，后者与本词族并非同族。

items.example: The prefix marks a repeated application.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出反复施加。

items.example: The root carries the image of medical care.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着医疗照护的意象。
remedium 是被施加的那个东西。

items.example: The remedy was rest and clean water.
items.exampleCN: 治疗之物是休息与干净的水。

items.example: The suffix turns the cure into a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把治疗变成过程。

items.meaning: the act of curing or correcting
items.example: Remediation of the site began in spring.

items.exampleCN: 他们修复了受污染的土壤。
这个缺陷是可以补救的。

latinEntries.structure: medius, media, medium (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 概念框架；研究者把相关概念及其关系组织起来、用以界定范围并指导分析的结构
definition_en: a researcher's organized map of the concepts relevant to a study and the relationships among them
core_image: 白板上画着一圈圈方框，每个框里写一个概念，箭头把彼此的关系连起来，最后收束成一个整体
scene: 做质性研究的学生把访谈里反复出现的几类现象先画成方框，再用箭头标出它们的关系。 The conceptual framework shows how the three factors influence one another.
sceneCN: 这里指用图示把概念与关系组织起来的框架（第 1 个义项：概念及其关系的组织图）；句意为这个概念框架显示了三个因素之间如何相互影响。

derivatives.zh: 拉丁语「 conceive」而来的名词，义为「概念」
由「概念」加形容词尾构成，义为「概念的」
加动词尾，义为「概念化；把……形成概念」
再加表示行为的名词尾，义为「概念化过程」
加副词尾，义为「在概念上」

senses.title: A map of concepts and their links
senses.definition: a diagram or scheme that places the key concepts of a study and draws the links between them
senses.definitionCN: 把研究的关键概念摆出来并画出彼此关系的图式或方案
senses.example: The conceptual framework places trust between communication and cooperation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把信任放在沟通与合作之间。
senses.why: A map is not the land, but it fixes which places connect, and the phrase does exactly that for ideas.
senses.whyCN: 地图不是土地，却固定了哪些地方相连，这个词组对观念做的正是这件事。

senses.title: The researcher's own synthesis
senses.definition: the arrangement the researcher builds from the literature rather than a scheme borrowed whole
senses.definitionCN: 研究者从文献中自行搭建的安排，而非整套搬用的方案
senses.example: Her conceptual framework grew out of five years of field notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她的概念框架是从五年的田野笔记里长出来的。
senses.why: Theoretical frameworks are borrowed, but conceptual ones are assembled, which is why the possessive «her» matters.
senses.whyCN: 理论框架是借的，概念框架是拼的，所以这里用「她的」来限定。

senses.title: A diagram of the variables
senses.definition: a visual arrangement of variables and arrows that shows expected directions of influence
senses.definitionCN: 把变量与箭头排成图，显示预期的影响方向
senses.example: The conceptual framework puts the mediator in the middle of the diagram.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把中介变量放在图示中央。
senses.why: Arrows carry direction, and a framework drawn with arrows reads almost like a claim about cause.
senses.whyCN: 箭头带方向，用箭头画出的框架读起来几乎就是对因果的主张。

senses.title: The set of constructs to be measured
senses.definition: the defined constructs that the study will turn into measures or interview codes
senses.definitionCN: 研究将转化为测量指标或访谈编码的、已界定的构念
senses.example: Each box in the conceptual framework became a scale in the questionnaire.
senses.exampleCN: 概念框架里的每个方框都变成了问卷中的一张量表。
senses.why: What is drawn must eventually be measured, so the framework also lists the constructs that need instruments.
senses.whyCN: 画出来的东西最终要能被测量，因此框架也列出需要工具去测的构念。

senses.title: The scheme for coding qualitative data
senses.definition: the analytic scheme that guides how interviews or observations are sorted into categories
senses.definitionCN: 指导如何把访谈或观察归入各类别的分析方案
senses.example: The coder used the conceptual framework to group the responses.
senses.exampleCN: 编码员用这个概念框架给回答分组。
senses.why: In qualitative work the framework becomes a set of boxes that the raw talk is sorted into.
senses.whyCN: 在质性研究里，框架变成一组方框，原始话语被分装进去。

senses.title: The stated scope of the study
senses.definition: the boundary that the framework draws around what the study will and will not examine
senses.definitionCN: 框架为研究划定考察与不考察范围的边界
senses.example: The conceptual framework excludes firms with fewer than ten staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这个概念框架把不足十人的企业排除在外。
senses.why: A frame has edges, and stating the concepts also states what is left outside them.
senses.whyCN: 框有边，界定概念的同时也界定了框外之物。

senses.title: The framework section of a proposal
senses.titleCN: 研究计划中的框架部分
senses.definition: the written part of a proposal that presents and justifies the concept map
senses.definitionCN: 研究计划中呈现并论证概念图的书面部分
senses.example: The conceptual framework takes four pages of the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 概念框架在研究计划里占了四页。
senses.why: A drawing needs a caption, and academic writing turns the drawing into a named section.
senses.whyCN: 图需要说明文字，学术写作便把这张图变成一个具名章节。

senses.title: A guide for programme design
senses.definition: the concept scheme used to plan a policy, service or intervention outside pure research
senses.definitionCN: 用于在纯研究之外规划政策、服务或干预的概念方案
senses.example: The agency adopted the conceptual framework when it redesigned the service.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构在重新设计服务时采用了这个概念框架。
senses.why: The same map that organizes research can organize action, because both need to know which factors connect.
senses.whyCN: 组织研究的那张图也能组织行动，因为两者都需要知道哪些因素相连。

intro.en: Conceptual framework joins a Latin word for a conceived idea with an English word for a supporting structure. It names the map a researcher builds before the measuring begins.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语中表示「被构想出的观念」的词，与英语中表示承重结构的词接在一起，指研究者在开始测量之前搭好的那张图。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and with the prefix com- it produced concipere, to take in and conceive.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「拿、抓」，加上表示「共同」的前缀后构成「收进、孕育」，即构想。

items.en: Conceptus named a taking in, hence a conceived idea; English concept arrived through French in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 这个词指「收进」，因而指被构想出的观念；英语的「概念」经法语在十六世纪进入。

items.en: The adjective conceptual appeared in the seventeenth century for what exists in the mind rather than in the hand.
items.cn: 形容词「概念的」在十七世纪出现，指存在于头脑而非手中的东西。

items.en: Frame named a structure that gives shape and support, and its verb meant to construct.
items.cn: 这个词指给出形状与支撑的结构，其动词义为建造。

items.en: The compound appeared in the sixteenth or seventeenth century for a skeletal support; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十六或十七世纪出现，指骨架式的支撑；确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: Research methods texts fixed conceptual framework as the researcher's own map, distinct from a borrowed theoretical framework.
items.cn: 研究方法教材把「概念框架」固定为研究者自绘的图，与借用的「理论框架」相区别。

note.en: The first group belongs to the concept family or looks similar; the second group names neighbouring research structures.
note.cn: 第一组属于「概念」同族或形近；第二组指相邻的研究结构。

entries.definition: A general idea formed by taking the shared features of many cases.
entries.definitionCN: 指从众多事例的共同点中形成的一般观念。

entries.definition: Existing in thought or organized around concepts.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在于思想中或以概念组织的。

entries.definition: To form a concept of something or to describe it in conceptual terms.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物形成概念或以概念方式描述。

entries.definition: The act of forming an idea, or the idea formed.
entries.definitionCN: 指形成观念的行为或所形成的观念。

entries.definition: A supporting structure, physical or conceptual.
entries.definitionCN: 指支撑结构，可为实物或概念。

entries.definition: To leave out; it looks like concept but comes from a taking-out prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指排除在外；形近但来自「取出」的前缀。

entries.definition: A theory structure borrowed from a field, which a study then applies.
entries.definitionCN: 指从某一领域借来、由研究加以应用的理论结构。

entries.definition: The structure that shows how a problem will be broken into analysable parts.
entries.definitionCN: 指显示如何把问题拆成可分析部分的结构。

entries.definition: A simplified formal representation of variables and their paths.
entries.definitionCN: 指变量及其路径的简化形式表示。

entries.definition: A field-wide way of thinking, broader than a single study's map.
entries.definitionCN: 指领域层面的整套思维方式，比单项研究的图更宽。

entries.definition: A defined attribute that a study intends to measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究打算测量的、已界定的属性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the whiteboard picture, the real distinction from a theoretical framework, and the measurement link.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用白板画图的画面、与理论框架的真实区别，以及通向测量的一环。

normal.en: Concept gives the boxes; framework gives the arrows and the edges.
normal.cn: 概念提供方框，框架提供箭头与边界。

normal.en: Conceptual frameworks are built, not borrowed, which is why they belong to a named researcher.
normal.cn: 概念框架是搭建的而非借用的，所以它属于某个具体研究者。

normal.en: Every box on the board should later become a measure, a code or a hypothesis.
normal.cn: 板上的每个方框后来都该变成一项测量、一个编码或一条假设。

normal.en: The theoretical framework supplies the theory; the conceptual framework supplies the arrangement.
normal.cn: 理论框架提供理论，概念框架提供排列方式。

normal.en: A map with arrows already whispers a claim about which way influence runs.
normal.cn: 带箭头的图已经在暗示影响朝哪个方向流动。

abstract.en: A conceptual framework is a promise that everything drawn will eventually be either measured or explained.
abstract.cn: 概念框架是一份承诺：画出的每样东西最终要么被测量，要么被解释。

abstract.en: Two researchers can share the same theory and still draw different maps, which shows the map is the person.
abstract.cn: 两位研究者可以共用一套理论却画出不同的图，说明图就是人本身。

abstract.en: The frame is drawn before the evidence arrives, and that order is what makes it a frame rather than a summary.
abstract.cn: 框架在证据到来之前就画好，正是这个顺序使它成为框架而不是总结。

examples.en: The conceptual framework groups motivation, opportunity and ability under one scheme.
examples.cn: 这个概念框架把动机、机会与能力归入同一套方案。

examples.en: She revised the conceptual framework after the first round of interviews.
examples.cn: 第一轮访谈之后，她修订了概念框架。

examples.en: The diagram in the conceptual framework became the basis for the questionnaire.
examples.cn: 概念框架中的图示成了问卷设计的基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「概念」是框里的字，「框架」是框本身：把概念装进框、用箭头连起来，就是概念框架

root: 「概念」源自拉丁语 concipere「收进、孕育」，其词根为 capere「抓取」；「框架」由古英语 framian「有用、推进」与 work 合成。二十世纪研究方法文献把「概念框架」固定为研究者自绘的概念关系图。最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the map itself to its practical uses: the concept map, the researcher's synthesis, the variable diagram, the constructs to measure, the coding scheme, the scope, the proposal section, and the design guide.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从图本身走向实际用途：概念关系图、研究者的综合、变量图示、待测构念、编码方案、研究范围、计划章节、设计指南。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boxes are drawn on a board and arrows are added until the separate ideas read as one structure.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上先画方框，再补箭头，直到分开的观念读起来像一个整体。

branches.en: THE BUILT MAP: concepts placed and linked by the researcher's own synthesis.
branches.cn: 搭建的图：由研究者自行综合摆放并连接的概念。

branches.en: THE ARROWED DIAGRAM: variables arranged with expected directions of influence.
branches.cn: 带箭头的图：变量按预期影响方向排列。

branches.en: THE MEASURABLE SIDE: constructs turned into scales and codes.
branches.cn: 可测量的一面：构念转化为量表与编码。

branches.en: THE STATED EDGES: the scope that is drawn and then written into the proposal.
branches.cn: 明示的边缘：画出范围，再写进研究计划。

branches.en: THE OUTWARD USE: the same map guiding a service or policy design.
branches.cn: 向外的用途：同一张图指导服务或政策设计。

intro.en: Conceptual framework joins a Latin idea word to an Old English structure word; both halves keep their original pictures.
intro.cn: 这个词组把拉丁语的观念词与古英语的结构词接起来，两半都保留着原始画面。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies concipere and conceptus; the structure half is native English and has no Latin entry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「构想」与「概念」两词；结构那一半是英语本族词，没有拉丁语条目。

items.example: It turns taking into taking in.
The root behind concept and capture.
items.exampleCN: 这是「概念」与「捕获」共同的词根。

items.example: The direct source of the idea word.
items.exampleCN: 这是观念词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms conceptual from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由名词构成形容词「概念的」。

items.example: The load-bearing half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是词组里承重的那一半。

items.example: It joins frame to make framework.
The verb built on the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是由该形容词构成的动词。

definition_zh: 个人主义的；强调个体独立与个性的；我行我素的
definition_en: favouring individual independence and personal choice over collective authority; also showing a distinctive personal style that resists group pressure
core_image: 整齐的队伍向前走，只有一个人拐向自己的小路
scene: 这里指「个人主义的」。 His individualistic streak made him reject the team's uniform schedule and design his own research plan. Colleagues found him difficult, yet the plan eventually won the prize.
sceneCN: 这里 individualistic 是「强调自立自主的」（第 2 个义项：行为上独立自主）；句意：他那种我行我素的性格使他拒绝团队统一的日程，自行设计了研究方案；同事们觉得他难相处，但方案最终获了奖。图中可辨识物件：队伍、独自的小路、研究笔记、奖杯。

pos.zh: 个人主义的；强调个体独立的；我行我素的

senses.title: Holding that the individual comes before the group
senses.titleCN: 个人主义（学说）：个体先于群体
senses.definition: believing that individual independence and personal interests should take priority over collective authority
senses.definitionCN: 认为个体的独立与个人利益应优先于集体权威的
senses.example: The party's individualistic philosophy opposed any plan that assigned people to collective farms.
senses.exampleCN: 该党的个人主义理念反对任何把人分配到集体农场的计划。
senses.why: Latin individuus means 'not divisible': the individual is the atom that cannot be split. A doctrine that makes this atom the starting point of politics is literally individualistic, and -istic marks adherence to a doctrine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 individuus 意为「不可分的」：个体是不可再分的原子。把这一原子当作政治出发点的学说，字面上就是 individualistic，而 -istic 标记对学说的归属。

senses.title: Acting independently rather than relying on the group
senses.definition: showing a habit of making one's own decisions and acting without depending on others
senses.definitionCN: 表现出自行决定、不依赖他人而行动的习惯
senses.example: She had an individualistic working style and rarely asked for guidance.
senses.exampleCN: 她的工作风格很自主，很少请求指导。
senses.why: If the individual is the indivisible unit, then individualistic conduct treats one's own judgment as the unit of decision and refuses to dissolve it into the group's judgment.
senses.whyCN: 如果个体是不可分的单位，那么 individualistic 行为就把自己的判断当作决策单位，拒绝把它溶入群体的判断。

senses.title: Expressing a distinctive personal style
senses.definition: marked by a personal style or taste that deliberately avoids following the crowd
senses.definitionCN: 带有刻意不随大流的个人风格或品味的
senses.example: His individualistic dress made him easy to spot at any conference.
senses.exampleCN: 他独特的穿着使他在任何会议上都容易被认出。
senses.why: The image shifts from 'cannot be divided' to 'cannot be merged': a style that refuses to be absorbed into a common style is individualistic.
senses.whyCN: 意象从「不可分」转为「不可融合」：拒绝被吸收进共同风格的风格，就是 individualistic。

senses.title: Stressing private initiative in economic life
senses.titleCN: 经济上强调个人自主经营
senses.definition: favouring private initiative, personal ownership, and market choices over collective economic control
senses.definitionCN: 主张私人创业、个人所有权和市场选择，而非集体经济控制的
senses.example: The country moved from an individualistic farm economy to large cooperatives within a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在十年内从个人自主的农业经济转向大型合作社。
senses.why: Economics took the indivisible individual as its basic unit of decision. An individualistic economy is one built from many such units rather than from one collective planner.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把不可分的个体当作基本决策单位。个人主义经济就是由许多这样的单位、而非由一个集体计划者搭建起来的经济。

senses.title: Explaining social facts through individuals
senses.titleCN: 方法论上以个体为解释单位
senses.definition: relating to a method that explains collective behaviour by tracing it back to individual choices
senses.definitionCN: 与把集体行为追溯至个体选择来解释的方法相关的
senses.example: The sociologist took an individualistic view of voting patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 这位社会学家以个体主义的视角看待投票模式。
senses.why: The same atom image becomes a research rule: if society is made of indivisible individuals, then collective facts should be explained from individual decisions upward.
senses.whyCN: 同一个原子意象变成研究规则：如果社会由不可分的个体组成，那么集体事实就应自下而上地由个体决策来解释。

senses.title: Selfish or indifferent to others
senses.definition: caring mainly about one's own advantage and showing little concern for other people
senses.definitionCN: 主要关心自身利益、很少顾及他人的
senses.example: Voters rejected an individualistic housing policy that left poorer families to fend for themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 选民否决了一项让较贫困家庭自行谋生的个人主义住房政策。
senses.why: When the boundary around the indivisible self hardens into a wall, independence becomes indifference. The negative sense grows from the same root image of a unit that will not merge.
senses.whyCN: 当不可分的自我边界凝固成墙时，独立就变成冷漠。贬义正是从「不肯融合的单位」这一同一词根意象生长出来的。

senses.title: Giving personal rights priority over the state
senses.titleCN: 政治上个人权利优先于国家
senses.definition: holding that personal rights and freedoms should limit what the state may require of a citizen
senses.definitionCN: 主张个人权利与自由应限制国家对公民的要求的
senses.example: The constitution reflects an individualistic distrust of unchecked state power.
senses.exampleCN: 这部宪法反映出一种个人主义的、对不受制约的国家权力的不信任。
senses.why: The state is a larger body made of citizens; individualistic politics insists that the smaller indivisible unit cannot be absorbed by the larger one. The prefix in- 'not' keeps the unit from being divided into the state.
senses.whyCN: 国家是由公民组成的更大整体；个人主义政治坚持较小的不可分单位不能被较大整体吞并。否定前缀 in-「不」使这个单位不被分割进国家。

senses.title: A culture that rewards personal achievement
senses.titleCN: 崇尚个人成就的文化特征
senses.definition: describing a culture in which personal achievement and self-expression are valued above group loyalty
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种把个人成就与自我表达看得高于群体忠诚的文化
senses.example: Cross-cultural studies often contrast individualistic cultures with collectivist ones.
senses.exampleCN: 跨文化研究常把个人主义文化与集体主义文化相对照。
senses.why: Cultures differ in what they treat as the unit of society. Where the indivisible individual is the unit, achievement is measured person by person, and that pattern is called individualistic.
senses.whyCN: 不同文化对社会单位的设定不同。在把不可分个体当作单位的地方，成就按人逐一衡量，这种模式就被称为 individualistic。

senses.title: Playing alone instead of with the team
senses.titleCN: 球场上单打独斗、缺乏配合
senses.definition: in sport, tending to keep the ball and act alone rather than combine with teammates
senses.definitionCN: 在体育中倾向于控球单干、不与队友配合的
senses.example: The coach benched the talented but individualistic winger.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把那位有天赋但爱单干的边锋放到替补席。
senses.why: A team is a whole made of parts; the individualistic player treats himself as a unit that need not merge with the passing pattern. The same 'will not merge' idea appears in a purely physical setting.
senses.whyCN: 团队是由部分组成的整体；个人主义的球员把自己当作无需融入传球配合的单位。同一个「不肯融合」的观念出现在纯身体性的场景中。

intro.en: Individualistic is an English adjective built on individual, which goes back through medieval Latin individualis to Latin individuus 'not divisible'. The suffix -istic reached English through French -istique and Greek -istikos.
intro.cn: individualistic 是在 individual 上构成的英语形容词；individual 经中世纪拉丁 individualis 上溯到拉丁 individuus「不可分的」。后缀 -istic 经法语 -istique 和希腊 -istikos 进入英语。

items.en: dividere meant 'to divide, separate'. Its root is a verb of splitting, so anything built with it starts from the image of cutting a whole apart.
items.cn: dividere 意为「分开、分离」。它的词根是一个表示劈开的动词，因此由它构成的词都从「把整体切开」这一画面出发。

items.en: in- 'not' + dividere produced individuus 'not divisible, inseparable'. Latin used it of atoms and of persons: the smallest thing that cannot be cut further.
items.cn: in-「不」+ dividere 构成 individuus「不可分的、不可分离的」。拉丁语用它指原子，也指人：不能再被切开的最小单位。

items.en: Schoolmen formed individualis to mean 'single, belonging to one indivisible entity'. This is the direct source of English individual.
items.cn: 经院学者构成 individualis，意为「单一的、属于一个不可分实体的」。这是英语 individual 的直接来源。

items.en: English took the word in the 15th century as an adjective and by the 17th century used it as a noun for a single person. The idea of the unmergeable unit was now a social word.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借入作形容词，到 17 世纪又用作名词指单个的人。不可融合的单位这一观念由此成为社会用语。

items.en: Greek -istikos meant 'skilled in, pertaining to'; through French -istique it became English -istic, the adjective suffix attached to -ism nouns. It marks adherence to a doctrine or tendency.
items.cn: 希腊 -istikos 意为「精于某事的、与某事相关的」；经法语 -istique 变成英语 -istic，是加在 -ism 名词上的形容词后缀，标记对某种学说或倾向的归属。

items.en: Individualistic is generally dated to the 19th century, when sociology and economics began contrasting individualist with collectivist societies. The exact first coinage is uncertain, but the formation is transparent.
items.cn: individualistic 一般认为是 19 世纪的产物，当时社会学和经济学开始把个人主义社会与集体主义社会对照。最早的确切用例已难考，但构词方式清楚。

note.en: Group one shares the Latin base individuus and differs only in suffix; group two is close in meaning but comes from other roots (Greek idios, Latin ego).
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁词基 individuus，差别只在后缀；第二组意义相近，但分别来自其他词根（希腊 idios、拉丁 ego）。

entries.definition: a single person or thing, or relating to one person; from Latin individuus 'not divisible'
entries.definitionCN: 单个的人或物；关于一个人的；来自拉丁 individuus「不可分的」

entries.definition: the belief that individual independence and interests should come first; -ism names the system of ideas, not the adjective
entries.definitionCN: 认为个体独立与利益应优先的信念；-ism 命名观念体系，并非形容词

entries.definition: a person who holds or lives by individualism; -ist marks the person, while -istic marks the quality
entries.definitionCN: 持有或践行个人主义的人；-ist 标记人，-istic 标记性质

entries.definition: the set of qualities that make a person distinct; built on individual with -ity, and not tied to any doctrine
entries.definitionCN: 使一个人与众不同的特质总和；由 individual 加 -ity 构成，与学说无关

entries.definition: not relying on or controlled by others; close to the self-reliance sense but says nothing about a doctrine
entries.definitionCN: 不依赖或不受他人控制的；接近自立义，但不涉及学说

entries.definition: able to act and decide without help from others; the behavioural core of the second sense
entries.definitionCN: 能无需他人帮助而行动和决定的；第 2 个义项的行为核心

entries.definition: oddly or strikingly personal in behaviour or style; from Greek idios 'one's own' + syn 'with' + krasis 'mixture', not from Latin individuus
entries.definitionCN: 行为或风格上奇特而个人的；来自希腊 idios「自己的」+ syn「一起」+ krasis「混合」，并非拉丁 individuus

entries.definition: centred on one's own interests; from Latin ego 'I', a different root from individuus
entries.definitionCN: 以自身利益为中心的；来自拉丁 ego「我」，与 individuus 词根不同

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real word relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分和真实同族词。

normal.en: in- 'not' + dividere 'to divide': the individual is the unit that cannot be divided any further.
normal.cn: in-「不」+ dividere「分开」：个体就是不能再被分割的单位。

normal.en: -istic is the adjective partner of -ism, as in realism → realistic; individualism is the doctrine, individualistic is its colour.
normal.cn: -istic 是 -ism 的形容词搭档，如 realism → realistic；individualism 是学说，individualistic 是它的色调。

normal.en: individual is the base; individuality is what makes each individual distinct; individualistic says that this distinctness should guide conduct.
normal.cn: individual 是基础词；individuality 是使每个个体独特的东西；individualistic 则说这种独特性应当指导行为。

normal.en: Think of a crowd moving as one mass: the individualistic person is the dot that refuses to be dissolved into the mass.
normal.cn: 想象一群人以一个整体移动：个人主义的人就是那颗拒绝被溶入整体的点。

normal.en: The pair individualistic / collectivist marks two ends of a scale in social description, and the suffixes -istic / -ist show the same pattern.
normal.cn: individualistic 与 collectivist 在社会描述中标出两个端点，后缀 -istic / -ist 呈现同一模式。

abstract.en: Think of an atom: it is called 'indivisible' precisely because every attempt to cut it fails, and individualistic thought treats the person the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一个原子：它被称为「不可分」，正因为每次切割都失败；个人主义思想也这样对待个人。

abstract.en: Picture a grid of dots: institutions draw lines between them, but the individualistic dot insists that the lines are optional.
abstract.cn: 想象一张点阵：制度在点与点之间画线，而个人主义的点坚持这些线是可选的。

abstract.en: Think of the suffix as a lens: -ism shows the belief, -ist shows the believer, and -istic shows the colour the belief gives to a life.
abstract.cn: 把后缀当作镜片：-ism 显示信念，-ist 显示信者，-istic 显示这信念给生活染上的颜色。

examples.en: American culture is often described as individualistic, stressing personal achievement over group loyalty.
examples.cn: 美国文化常被描述为个人主义的，强调个人成就高于群体忠诚。

examples.en: His individualistic approach to research produced a method that no one else could copy.
examples.cn: 他那种个人主义的研究方式产生了一套别人无法复制的方法。

examples.en: Critics say the reform is too individualistic and ignores collective bargaining.
examples.cn: 批评者说这项改革过于个人主义，忽视了集体谈判。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词联想 · 词源辅助
dict_mnemonic.text: in-（不）+ dividere（分开）→ individuus 不可分的 → individual 个体；-istic 表学说与倾向 → individualistic 以个体为中心、个人主义的

root: 拉丁 dividere「分开」加否定前缀 in- 构成 individuus「不可分的」，经中世纪拉丁 individualis 形成 individual，再加经法语 -istique / 希腊 -istikos 而来的 -istic；核心是「不可再分的个体」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one image: the individual is the smallest unit that cannot be divided, so a doctrine, a style, or a method that starts from that unit is individualistic.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一个意象辐射开来：个体是不可再分的最小单位，因此以这个单位为出发点的学说、风格或方法都是 individualistic。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the smallest unit that cannot be cut any further, standing on its own.
core.cn: 核心意象：不能再被切开、独自站立的最小单位。

branches.en: THE DOCTRINE: individual independence and interests are treated as the starting point of social life.
branches.cn: 学说：把个体独立与利益当作社会生活的出发点。

branches.en: CONDUCT: the same unit becomes self-reliance when respected, and selfishness when it hardens into a wall.
branches.cn: 行为：同一个单位被尊重时表现为自立，凝固成墙时表现为自私。

branches.en: STYLE AND GROUP FRICTION: personal taste, a culture of achievement, and the player who will not pass the ball.
branches.cn: 风格与群体摩擦：个人品味、崇尚成就的文化，以及不肯传球的球员。

branches.en: ECONOMY AND POLITICS: systems built on the independent individual as the basic unit.
branches.cn: 经济与政治：以独立个体为基本单位来搭建的制度。

branches.en: METHOD: collective facts are explained by tracing them back to individual decisions.
branches.cn: 方法：把集体事实追溯回个体决策来解释。

intro.en: Individualistic is individual plus the adjective suffix -istic, which descends from Greek -istikos through French -istique. The negative prefix in- and the verb dividere are fossilized inside the base.
intro.cn: individualistic 是 individual 加形容词后缀 -istic 构成，-istic 经法语 -istique 上溯希腊 -istikos。否定前缀 in- 与动词 dividere 已凝固在词基内部。

latinIntro.en: Latin dividere 'to divide' built a family: divide, division, individual, indivisible, subdivide, dividend. The root appears as divid-, divis-, or vid-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dividere「分开」构成了一个词族：divide、division、individual、indivisible、subdivide、dividend。词根以 divid-、divis- 或 vid- 形式出现。
