definition_zh: 冲动；突发的行动欲望；推动力；刺激；[物理] 冲量；[神经] 神经冲动；[电子] 脉冲
definition_en: a sudden urge to act, or a force that drives something forward
core_image: 一只手刚要伸向橱窗里的蛋糕，另一只手在手腕上轻轻按住
scene: 商场橱窗前，一个人原本只想路过， An impulse made him stop and buy the cake in the window.
sceneCN: 这里 impulse 指「突然想做某事的冲动」（第 1 个义项：突发的行动欲望）；句意为一股冲动让他停下来买橱窗里的蛋糕。图中可辨识物件：橱窗、蛋糕、购物袋、玻璃反光。

pos.zh: 冲动；突发的欲望；推动力；冲量；神经冲动；脉冲

senses.title: A sudden urge to act
senses.definition: a sudden strong wish to do something, often without planning
senses.definitionCN: 突然产生的强烈行动欲望，常未经计划
senses.example: She felt an impulse to laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然想笑。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to drive against, so the urge arrives like a push from inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「朝前推」，因此冲动像从身体内部推来的一股力。

senses.title: A push or stimulus from outside
senses.titleCN: 来自外部的推动或刺激
senses.definition: a force or stimulus that drives something to move or respond
senses.definitionCN: 促使某物移动或作出反应的力量或刺激
senses.example: The first impulse came from the crowd outside.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的推动来自外面的人群。
senses.why: The push need not begin inside a person; any external force that starts a movement is an impulse.
senses.whyCN: 推力不必起于人的内部；任何引发运动的外力都是冲量意义上的推动。

senses.title: Force multiplied by time in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理中力与时间的乘积
senses.definition: in physics, the product of a force and the time during which it acts
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中，一个力与它作用时间的乘积
senses.example: The impulse changed the cart's momentum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个冲量改变了小车的动量。
senses.why: Physics measures a push by how long it lasts, so the word becomes a precise quantity.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用推力持续多久来度量推，于是这个词成了一个精确的量。

senses.title: A signal travelling along a nerve
senses.definition: a brief electrical change that travels along a nerve fibre
senses.definitionCN: 沿神经纤维传导的短暂电变化
senses.example: The nerve carries impulses from the finger to the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 神经把冲动从手指传到脊柱。
senses.why: A signal is a short burst of driving force, so physiology borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 信号是一小段驱动力的爆发，因此生理学也借用了这个词。

senses.title: A short burst of signal in electronics
senses.titleCN: 电子学中的短促信号脉冲
senses.definition: a short sudden change in voltage or current, used to carry information
senses.definitionCN: 电压或电流的短促突变，用来承载信息
senses.example: Each key sends an impulse to the circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 每按一个键，都会向电路发出一个脉冲。
senses.why: The physical push shrinks to a brief burst, and the word follows it into circuitry.
senses.whyCN: 物理的推力缩小成一次短暂爆发，这个词便跟着进入电路。

senses.title: A purchase made without planning
senses.definition: a purchase made suddenly, without prior planning
senses.definitionCN: 没有事先计划、突然作出的购买
senses.example: The chocolates were an impulse at the checkout.
senses.exampleCN: 这些巧克力是结账时一时冲动买的。
senses.why: Commerce names the urge by its result, so the bought thing becomes an impulse.
senses.whyCN: 商业用结果来命名欲望，于是被买下的东西本身就成了「冲动」。

senses.title: The drive behind creative work
senses.definition: a strong inner drive that leads to creative work
senses.definitionCN: 促使人创作作品的强烈内在驱动
senses.example: He painted from an impulse rather than a plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他作画是凭一股冲动，而不是按计划。
senses.why: The surge that moves the hand can also move the brush, and art calls it an impulse.
senses.whyCN: 推动手的那股涌动也能推动画笔，艺术便称之为冲动。

senses.title: The drive behind behaviour
senses.definition: in psychology, an inner force that pushes a person toward action
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中，促使人行动的内在力量
senses.example: The therapist traced the impulse behind his spending.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师追溯他消费行为背后的驱力。
senses.why: Psychology formalizes the push as a drive, keeping the physics of motion inside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把这股推力正式化为驱力，把运动的物理留在了心里。

intro.en: Impulse comes from Latin impulsus, a noun of action from impellere, to drive into or against. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: impulse 来自拉丁语 impulsus，是动词 impellere 的动名词，后者意为「推入、推向」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pellere meant to push or drive. Its older Indo-European source is reconstructed as a root meaning to thrust or strike, and that form is not recorded.
items.cn: pellere 意为「推、驱动」。它更早的印欧语来源被重构为一个表示「推、击」的词根，该词形没有记录。

items.en: In- meaning into plus pellere produced impellere, to drive into or against something.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 pellere 构成 impellere，意为「推入、撞向某物」。

items.en: The noun impulsus named a push or a shock, and classical Latin already used it for both physical and mental driving.
items.cn: 名词 impulsus 指推击或冲击，古典拉丁语已用它兼指物理与心理上的驱动。

items.en: English adopted impulse in the sixteenth century, first as a physical push and soon after as a sudden urge.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪引入 impulse，先指物理的推击，很快又指突然的欲望。

items.en: Physics, physiology and electronics each gave the word a precise technical sense from the nineteenth century onward.
items.cn: 物理学、生理学与电子学从十九世纪起各自赋予这个词一个精确的技术义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, and the pre-Latin root of pellere is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语最早书证年代无定论；pellere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式，并非有记录的真实词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb pellere but differs in prefix; the second holds words for urges and driving forces. One look-alike comes from a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 pellere，只是前缀不同；第二组是表示欲望与驱动力的词。有一个形似词来自不同词根。

entries.definition: To drive someone to act; it is the verb behind the noun impulse.
entries.definitionCN: 驱使某人行动；它正是名词 impulse 背后的动词。

entries.definition: Com- plus pellere: to drive together or force; it implies pressure that leaves little choice.
entries.definitionCN: com- 加 pellere：驱使到一处或强迫；它含几乎没有选择余地的压力。

entries.definition: Re- meaning back plus pellere: to drive away, as a surface drives off water.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 pellere：把东西推走，如同表面把水排开。

entries.definition: From Latin impetere, built on petere meaning to seek or attack, not pellere; it means momentum or driving force.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 impetere，词根是 petere「寻求、攻击」而非 pellere；意为势头或推动力。

entries.definition: A strong desire to do something; impulse adds the note of suddenness and of arriving without planning.
entries.definitionCN: 想做某事的强烈愿望；impulse 多了「突然」与「未经计划」两层意思。

entries.definition: A continuing force that keeps someone working; an impulse is usually a short burst.
entries.definitionCN: 使人持续工作的力量；impulse 通常是短促的一次爆发。

entries.definition: Something external that causes a response; impulse can also name the inner wish.
entries.definitionCN: 引起反应的外在事物；impulse 也可以指内在的欲望。

entries.definition: The force of a body already moving; an impulse is what starts or changes that motion.
entries.definitionCN: 已经在运动的物体所具有的力；impulse 是启动或改变该运动的推击。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the root of driving, the real family and the phrases the noun keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、表示「驱动」的词根、真实的同族词，以及这个名词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: in- meaning into plus pellere meaning drive: a push that enters and sets something moving.
normal.cn: in-「进入」加 pellere「驱动」：一股推进来，把东西带动起来。

normal.en: The family runs impulse, impel, impulsive, impulsively and impulsiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 impulse（冲动）、impel（推动）、impulsive（冲动的）、impulsively（冲动地）、impulsiveness（冲动性）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: on impulse, impulse buying, resist an impulse, act on impulse.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：一时冲动、冲动购买、克制冲动、凭冲动行事。

normal.en: Physics measures impulse as force times time, which makes the everyday push exact.
normal.cn: 物理学把冲量度量成力乘时间，让日常的「推」变得精确。

normal.en: Impetus looks like impulse but comes from seeking, not driving, so the roots differ.
normal.cn: impetus 看似与 impulse 同族，却来自「寻求」而不是「驱动」，词根并不相同。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for a cake and another hand holding the wrist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向蛋糕，另一只手按住了手腕。

abstract.en: Picture a short shove that sends a swing moving and then lets it coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一次短促的推，把秋千送出去，然后任它滑行。

abstract.en: Picture a spark crossing a gap for only a moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒火花只一瞬间穿过缝隙。

examples.en: He bought the guitar on impulse and never learned to play.
examples.cn: 他一时冲动买了那把吉他，却一直没学。

examples.en: Her first impulse was to deny everything.
examples.cn: 她的第一反应是把一切都否认掉。

examples.en: A nerve impulse travels faster than a spoken word can follow.
examples.cn: 神经冲动的传导比话语跟得上的速度还快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一木炮死」——一股劲突然推过来，人还没想就先动了 → impulse 冲动

root: 拉丁 impulsus「推击、冲击」来自 impellere = in-「进入」+ pellere「推、驱动」；pellere 更早的印欧语词根被重构为表示「推、击」的形式。英语 impulse 经法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a surge inside a person, a force from outside, a measured quantity in physics, a signal in a nerve, a burst in a circuit, a sudden purchase, a creative drive and a psychological drive.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次推动展开：人体内的一股涌动、外部的一股力、物理学里可度量的量、神经里的信号、电路里的爆发、突如其来的购买、创作上的驱动，以及心理上的驱力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand reaching for a cake while another hand presses the wrist down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手已经伸向蛋糕，另一只手把它的手腕按下去。

branches.en: URGE AND PURCHASE: the wish arrives suddenly and is sometimes named by the thing it bought.
branches.cn: 欲望与购买：愿望突然到来，有时又被它所买下的东西命名。

branches.en: PUSH AND DRIVE: an outside stimulus and an inner drive are the same force seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 推力与驱力：外在刺激与内在驱动是同一股力从两边看。

branches.en: MEASURED BURST: physics turns the push into force over time, and electronics into a pulse.
branches.cn: 可度量的爆发：物理学把推力变成力乘时间，电子学把它变成脉冲。

branches.en: NERVE SIGNAL: the body carries the same burst along a fibre.
branches.cn: 神经信号：身体把同样的爆发沿纤维传下去。

branches.en: CREATIVE DRIVE: the surge that moves a hand can also move a brush.
branches.cn: 创作驱动：推动手的那股涌动，也能推动画笔。

intro.en: Impulse can be read from a Latin prefix and a verb of driving that also build a wide English family.
intro.cn: impulse 可以按一个拉丁前缀与一个表示「驱动」的动词逐段读出，两者还构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere gives impel, compel, expel, repel and propel through related forms; in- adds direction into something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 通过相关形态衍生 impel、compel、expel、repel 与 propel；in- 加上「进入某物」的方向。

items.example: The prefix also appears in inject and invade.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也出现在 inject（注入）与 invade（侵入）里。

items.example: Its stem survives in propel and repel.
items.exampleCN: 它的词干留在 propel（推进）与 repel（击退）里。

items.meaning: a push, hence a sudden urge
items.meaningCN: 一推，因而指突然的冲动

items.meaning: the tendency to act on sudden urges
items.example: His impulsiveness cost him the job.
items.exampleCN: 他的冲动让他丢了工作。

derivatives.structure: impulse + -ive (tendency) → tending to follow a sudden push
impulsive + -ly (adverb) → in the manner of a sudden push
impulsive + -ness (quality) → the tendency to act on urges
in- into + pellere drive → to drive someone into action
com- strongly + pellere drive → to drive with force

definition_zh: 互惠；对等回应；国际间的对等；（社会）互惠规范；（数学）互易性；（法律）互惠待遇；情感上的对等；经济上的等价回报
definition_en: the practice of giving back to another what has been given, or of answering an act with a matching act
core_image: 两只手隔着桌子同时推过去一样分量的东西，谁也没有多拿，谁也没有先松手
scene: 边境口岸的谈判室里，两边代表把各自的关税清单推到桌子中央，谁也不肯先签字。 The treaty rests on reciprocity: each country lowers its tariff only if the other does the same.
sceneCN: 这里 reciprocity 指「你给什么、我也回什么的对等交换」（第 6 个义项：法律上的互惠待遇）；句意为条约以互惠为基础，一方降税以另一方同样降税为条件。可辨识物件：谈判长桌、两份关税清单、桌中央的文件夹、尚未落笔的签字页。

pos.zh: 互惠；对等；互易性（不可数，复数指多组对等关系）

forms.label: 形容词（倾向于回报的，少见）

derivatives.zh: 互惠的；对等的；（数学）倒数

senses.title: Giving back what was given
senses.definition: the general pattern in which a gift, favour or concession is answered with something of similar worth
senses.definitionCN: 泛指一方给出礼物、帮助或让步之后，另一方以价值相近之物回应的模式
senses.example: Long-distance trade among the villages depended on reciprocity rather than on money.
senses.exampleCN: 这些村落之间的远途贸易靠的是互惠，而不是货币。
senses.why: The Latin adjective behind the word described movement back and forth, so the core of the noun is a going and a returning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁形容词描述来回移动，因此这个名词的核心就是「去」与「回」。

senses.title: Answering an act in kind
senses.definition: responding to someone's gesture with a matching one, such as returning a smile, a greeting or a favour
senses.definitionCN: 以相称的举动回应他人的举动，例如回以一个微笑、一声问候或一次帮忙
senses.example: She offered a seat, and reciprocity came at once in the form of a shared umbrella.
senses.exampleCN: 她让出一个座位，对方立刻以共撑一把伞作为回应。
senses.why: At this scale reciprocity is not a contract but a reflex: the second gesture mirrors the first.
senses.whyCN: 在这个尺度上，互惠不是契约而是一种反射：第二个举动照出第一个举动。

senses.title: Equal treatment between states
senses.definition: the diplomatic rule that a state grants another the same treatment it receives, so that neither gains an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 外交规则：一国给予另一国它所得到的同等对待，使任何一方都不占优势
senses.example: Visa waivers were granted on a basis of strict reciprocity.
senses.exampleCN: 签证豁免是在严格对等的基础上给予的。
senses.why: Between sovereign states there is no higher authority, so equality has to be written into the exchange itself.
senses.whyCN: 主权国家之上没有更高的权威，因此平等只能写进交换本身。

senses.title: The unwritten norm of return
senses.definition: in sociology, the shared expectation that a favour will be returned, which holds groups together without formal enforcement
senses.definitionCN: 社会学中指「受助应当回报」的共同期待，它无需正式执行就能把群体维系起来
senses.example: The norm of reciprocity keeps neighbours shovelling each other's steps after a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 互惠规范让邻居们在暴风雪后互相铲除对方门前的雪。
senses.why: A community cannot police every favour, so it runs on a shared expectation that returns will come.
senses.whyCN: 社区无法对每一次帮忙都加以监督，于是靠一种共同期待运转：回报终会到来。

senses.title: A law that holds in both directions
senses.titleCN: 数学中双向成立的互易定律
senses.definition: in mathematics, a theorem showing that a relation between two objects holds equally when the two are exchanged, as in the quadratic reciprocity law
senses.definitionCN: 数学中指两个对象互换位置后关系仍同样成立的定理，如二次互反律
senses.example: The quadratic reciprocity law links pairs of primes in a way that works the same in either direction.
senses.exampleCN: 二次互反律把成对的素数联系起来，无论从哪一方看，关系都同样成立。
senses.why: Mathematics kept the back-and-forth image but made it a statement about symmetry rather than about trading favours.
senses.whyCN: 数学保留了「来回」的图景，却把它变成关于对称的命题，而不是关于互相帮忙。

senses.title: Reciprocal treatment under law
senses.definition: the legal arrangement by which a right or benefit granted to foreigners is conditional on the same right being granted at home
senses.definitionCN: 一种法律安排：给予外国人的权利或利益，以本国人在对方境内也获得同样权利为条件
senses.example: The treaty rests on reciprocity: each country lowers its tariff only if the other does the same.
senses.exampleCN: 条约以互惠为基础：一方降税以另一方同样降税为条件。
senses.why: Law makes the return a condition rather than a courtesy, so non-reciprocity becomes a ground for withdrawal.
senses.whyCN: 法律把回报设成条件而不是礼貌，因此不对等就成了撤回的理由。

senses.title: Feeling returned in equal measure
senses.definition: the state in which affection, trust or regard is felt on both sides in comparable degree
senses.definitionCN: 双方在相当程度上都怀有喜爱、信任或看重的情感状态
senses.example: What she valued was not reciprocity of gifts but reciprocity of regard.
senses.exampleCN: 她看重的不是礼物的对等，而是彼此看重的对等。
senses.why: The same exchange image applies to feeling, where what returns cannot be weighed but can still be missed.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅交换图景也适用于感情：回过来的东西无法称重，却仍能感到它的缺席。

senses.title: Equivalent return in economic exchange
senses.definition: in economics, the requirement that what flows back be of comparable value, whether in trade, aid or investment
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中指回流之物须具有相当价值的要求，无论涉及贸易、援助还是投资
senses.example: Aid without reciprocity can create lasting dependence rather than partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 没有等价回报的援助，可能造成长期依赖而不是伙伴关系。
senses.why: Economics turns the moral idea of fairness into a measurable condition of comparable value.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把公平这一道德观念，变成可衡量的「价值相当」条件。

intro.en: Reciprocity comes from French réciprocité, built on the adjective réciproque, which descends from Latin reciprocus 'moving back and forth, alternating'. The internal formation of reciprocus is not established: the common account joining re- 'back' to pro- 'forward' is a hypothesis, and no ancient source sets out the compound.
intro.cn: reciprocity 来自法语 réciprocité，由形容词 réciproque 构成，后者上溯到拉丁 reciprocus「往复的、交替的」。reciprocus 的内部构词并未得到确证：通常把它解释为 re-「回」加 pro-「向前」，但这只是一种假说，没有任何古代文献说明过这个词的构成。

items.en: Reciprocus described what moves back and forth or alternates between two points; it is the base of the whole English family.
items.cn: reciprocus 描述在两个端点之间来回移动或交替的事物；它是整个英语词族的基础。

items.en: Source uncertain: the familiar reading of the word as re- 'back' plus pro- 'forward' is a hypothesis, not a recorded derivation, and no other segmentation has been proven either.
items.cn: 来源不确定：把这个词读作 re-「回」加 pro-「向前」只是一种假说，并非有记录的派生过程，其他切分方式同样未获证明。

items.en: The verb reciprocare meant to move to and fro and also to give back in return; English reciprocate descends from it.
items.cn: 动词 reciprocare 意为「来回移动」，也指「回报」；英语的 reciprocate 由它而来。

items.en: French passed réciprocité, built on the adjective réciproque, to English, where reciprocity first named a relation that runs both ways between two parties.
items.cn: 法语把由形容词 réciproque 构成的 réciprocité 传给英语，reciprocity 最初指两方之间可双向成立的关系。

items.en: Treaties of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries made reciprocity a term of art in international law, while mathematics fixed the reciprocal as a product of one.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的条约使 reciprocity 成为国际法上的专门术语，而数学则把「倒数」固定为乘积为一的关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English use cannot be assigned to an exact year, and the pre-Latin history of reciprocus is a reconstruction with no agreed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：最早的英语用例无法系于确切年份；reciprocus 在拉丁语之前的历史属重构，没有公认的形式。

note.en: Group one holds the true relatives built on the Latin adjective of going back and forth, plus two look-alikes that descend from a different verb meaning to receive, and those two must not be confused with this family. Group two holds words for exchange that differ in formality and in whether equality is required.
note.cn: 第一组是同出那个表示「来回」的拉丁形容词的真正同源词，另加两个形近词；后者出自另一个意为「接收」的动词，绝不可与这一词族混为一谈。第二组是表示交换的词，区别在于正式程度以及是否要求对等。

entries.definition: The adjective from the same Latin base: describing something given or felt in return, and in mathematics the inverse of a quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这一拉丁词基的形容词：形容回报或回应的东西，在数学中指一个量的倒数。

entries.definition: The verb from the same base: to give or feel something in return, or of a machine, to move back and forth.
entries.definitionCN: 同出这一词基的动词：回报或回应某种情感；用于机器时指往复运动。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of returning something; it names one act, while reciprocity can name a standing relation between parties.
entries.definitionCN: 指「回报」这一动作的名词；它指一次动作，而 reciprocity 可指双方之间长期存在的关系。

entries.definition: From Latin recipere 'to receive', built on re- plus capere 'to take'; it names the one who receives and has nothing to do with returning anything.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 recipere「接收」，由 re- 加 capere「抓取」构成；它指接收者，与回报毫无关系。

entries.definition: Also from recipere, literally 'take this'; the shared opening syllables are misleading, since its root is the taking verb, not the back-and-forth adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 recipere，字面意为「取这些」；开头音节相同只是误导，它的词根是「抓取」动词，而不是那个表示来回的形容词。

entries.definition: Describing something held or felt by two parties at once, such as mutual respect; it states the sharing but not the rule of return.
entries.definitionCN: 形容两方同时拥有或感受到的东西，如相互尊重；它陈述共享，却不含回报规则。

entries.definition: The act of giving one thing and receiving another; it names the transaction, while reciprocity names the principle that the two sides balance.
entries.definitionCN: 给出一样并得到另一样的行为；它指交易本身，而 reciprocity 指两边应当平衡的原则。

entries.definition: A thing given in return for something specific, often with a legal or political flavour; it is the concrete instance, reciprocity the general rule.
entries.definitionCN: 为换取某一具体之物而给出的东西，常带法律或政治色彩；它是具体的一例，而 reciprocity 是一般规则。

entries.definition: An informal phrase for mutual concession in a relationship; it stresses willingness to bend, not exact equality.
entries.definitionCN: 指关系中互相让步的口语说法；它强调愿意退让，而不是精确对等。

entries.definition: A correspondence of parts on either side of a line or point; it describes shape and balance, not an obligation to return a favour.
entries.definitionCN: 指一条线或一个点两侧部分的对应；它描述形状与均衡，而不是回报人情的义务。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin base with its uncertain internal story, the genuine family, the two look-alikes from the receiving verb, and the legal and mathematical uses that fixed the term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词基及其未获确证的内部构成、真正的同族词、两个来自「接收」动词的形近词，以及让这个词定型的法律与数学用法。

normal.en: The Latin base describes movement back and forth, so reciprocity is a going out and a coming back, never a one-way gift.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁词基描述来回移动，所以互惠是「去」与「回」，绝不是单向的赠予。

normal.en: The internal division into back plus forward is only a hypothesis, so learn the whole base rather than a made-up root.
normal.cn: 把它切成「回」加「向前」只是假说，因此要记整个词基，而不是一个人为拼出的词根。

normal.en: The family runs reciprocal, reciprocally, reciprocate, reciprocation and reciprocative.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reciprocal、reciprocally、reciprocate、reciprocation 与 reciprocative。

normal.en: Recipient and recipe look similar but come from the verb meaning to receive, so they are not relatives of this family.
normal.cn: recipient 与 recipe 看着相似，却出自意为「接收」的动词，因此不是这个词族的同源词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the frame: on the basis of reciprocity, the principle of reciprocity, social reciprocity, expect reciprocity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出框架：在互惠基础上、互惠原则、社会互惠、期待对等回报。

abstract.en: Picture two doors facing each other across a courtyard, opening at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇隔着院子的门正对着，在同一刻同时打开。

abstract.en: Picture a scale with two identical pans, and neither side ever stays down for long.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆两边托盘一模一样的秤，没有哪一边能长久地压着。

abstract.en: Picture a ball thrown against a wall and coming back with the same force it was given.
abstract.cn: 想象一个球撞上墙，带着被扔出去时同样的力道弹回来。

examples.en: The scholarship scheme runs on reciprocity: graduates later fund a student of their own.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金以互惠方式运转：受助者毕业后再资助一名学生。

examples.en: Diplomats spoke of reciprocity rather than generosity, because each concession had to be matched.
examples.cn: 外交官谈的是对等而非慷慨，因为每一项让步都必须得到对等回应。

examples.en: In the algebra chapter, reciprocity simply means that a number and its inverse multiply to one.
examples.cn: 在代数那一章里，互易性只是指一个数与它的逆相乘为一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来回 + 相应」——东西送出去还要回得来，一分对一分，就是互惠与对等

root: 拉丁 reciprocus「往复的、交替的」，经法语 réciproque 进入英语。其内部构词来源不确定：一般认为与 re-（回）+ pro-（向前）有关，但这只是假说，并非有记录的派生，不得据此编造词根。同族的 reciprocal、reciprocate 出此词基；recipient、recipe 出 recipere = re- + capere「抓取」，与 reciprocus 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something goes out and something comes back. The return may be a gift, a mirrored gesture, a matching tariff, an unwritten social norm, an inverse in algebra, a legal condition, an equal affection, or a comparable economic value.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：有东西送出去，就有东西回来。回程之物可以是一份礼物、一个照做的举动、一项对等的关税、一条不成文的社会规范、代数里的逆、一项法律条件、一份对等的情感，或一种相当的经济价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands pushing equal things across a table at the same moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在同一刻把等分量的东西推过桌面。

branches.en: GIFT AND GESTURE: the everyday exchange, from a returned favour to a returned smile.
branches.cn: 礼物与举动：从回赠一份人情，到回以一个微笑的日常交换。

branches.en: BETWEEN POWERS: states and legal systems make the return a condition rather than a courtesy.
branches.cn: 权力之间：国家与法律体系把回报设成条件，而不是礼貌。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL NORM: no authority enforces it, yet the expectation of return holds the group together.
branches.cn: 社会规范：没有权威执行，然而「终会回报」的期待把群体维系在一起。

branches.en: THE EXACT INVERSE: algebra keeps the back-and-forth image and makes the return land on one.
branches.cn: 精确的逆：代数保留来回的图景，让回程落在「一」上。

branches.en: FEELING AND VALUE: what comes back can be regard that cannot be weighed, or money that must be.
branches.cn: 情感与价值：回过来的可以是无法称重的看重，也可以是必须称重的钱。

intro.en: Reciprocity is a Latin-derived noun whose base, verb and adjective endings are shared across a small but stable English family; its internal prefix story must be marked as uncertain.
intro.cn: reciprocity 是一个源自拉丁语的名词，其词基、动词与形容词词尾在一个小而稳定的英语词族中共享；其内部前缀的说法必须标为不确定。

latinIntro.en: Latin reciprocus supplies the back-and-forth image, reciprocare adds the verbal action of returning, and the noun ending turns the relation into a named principle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 reciprocus 提供「来回」的图景，reciprocare 添上「回报」这一动作，名词词尾则把这种关系变成一个被命名的原则。

items.example: This prefix is part of the usual but unproven reading of the base.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀属于对该词基通常却未获证明的读法。

items.example: The forward half of the image is proposed rather than recorded.
items.exampleCN: 图景中「向前」的那一半是推测出来的，而非有记录的。

items.example: The adjective names a movement that returns to where it started.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指一种回到起点的移动。

items.meaning: to move to and fro; to give in return
items.example: The verb turns the image into an action someone performs.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把图景变成某人可以执行的动作。

items.example: The treaty rests on reciprocity: each country lowers its tariff only if the other does the same.
items.exampleCN: 条约以互惠为基础：一方降税以另一方同样降税为条件。

items.example: The two universities signed a reciprocal agreement.
items.exampleCN: 两所大学签署了一份对等协议。

items.meaning: to return a favour or feeling
items.example: She reciprocated the invitation the following spring.
items.exampleCN: 次年春天她回请了对方。

items.example: His reciprocation was prompt and modest.
items.exampleCN: 他的回报既迅速又谦和。

latinEntries.structure: reciprocus, reciproca, reciprocum (adjective, first and second declension)

latinEntries.meaning: to move to and fro; to return

definition_zh: （皮肤的）老茧；硬结；（比喻）麻木不仁
definition_en: a hardened, thickened patch of skin; figuratively, unfeeling hardness of heart
core_image: 纤夫掌心一层磨不破的黄茧
scene: 老船夫摊开双手，掌心的茧硬如树皮。 Years of oars left a callosity across his palms.
sceneCN: 这里 callosity 是「老茧」（第 1 个义项：皮肤因摩擦而增厚变硬之处）；句意是多年摇桨在他掌上磨出厚茧。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「长老茧的；（心）冷酷的」
同根名词，义为「（皮肤或骨头的）胼胝、骨痂」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「冷酷地」

senses.title: A hardened patch of skin
senses.definition: a thickened, hardened area of skin formed by pressure or friction
senses.definitionCN: 因长期受压或摩擦而增厚变硬的皮肤区域
senses.example: The gardener's callosities told of forty seasons of labour.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁手上的老茧诉说着四十个耕作季节。
senses.why: Latin callum meant hard skin, and the suffix -ity names the condition.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 callum 意为硬皮，-ity 词尾标示这种状态。

senses.title: Any hardened swelling
senses.definition: a hard thickened spot or mass, as on a bone or plant
senses.definitionCN: 硬化的增厚处或硬块，如骨痂或植物愈伤组织
senses.example: The X-ray showed a callosity where the bone had knit.
senses.exampleCN: X 光片显示骨折处已结出骨痂。
senses.why: The hard-skin idea extends to bone and tissue healing.
senses.whyCN: 「硬皮」之意延伸到骨骼与组织的愈合。

senses.title: Unfeeling hardness of heart
senses.definition: insensibility to the feelings of others
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的痛苦无动于衷
senses.example: His reply showed the callosity of a man long past shame.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答显出一个久不知耻者的冷酷。
senses.why: Skin that feels nothing becomes a soul that feels nothing.
senses.whyCN: 无知觉的皮肤化为无知觉的心。

intro.en: Callosity comes from Latin callum, hard skin, plus the abstract suffix -itas.
intro.cn: callosity 由拉丁语 callum（硬皮）加抽象后缀 -itas 构成。

items.en: behind Latin callum lies a reconstructed root for hard or stony ground, uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 拉丁语 callum 背后是表示「硬、石质」的重构词根，细节不确定。

items.en: callum meant the hard skin of feet worn by walking.
items.cn: 拉丁语 callum 指因行走而磨硬的脚皮。

items.en: callositas named the state of being hardened.
items.cn: 拉丁语 callositas 指「硬化状态」。

items.en: callosity entered English for physical and then moral hardness.
items.cn: 十五至十六世纪 callosity 进入英语，先指身体硬化，后指心灵冷酷。

items.en: medical use prefers callus; callosity survives in literary and figurative writing.
items.cn: 医学上更常用 callus；callosity 留存于文学与比喻用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the hard-skin root; the near-meaning group lists insensitivity words.
note.cn: 形近组同出「硬皮」词根；近义组是麻木类词。

entries.definition: hardened; unfeeling
entries.definitionCN: 长老茧的；冷酷的

entries.definition: hardened skin or bone repair
entries.definitionCN: 胼胝；骨痂

entries.definition: in an unfeeling manner
entries.definitionCN: 冷酷地

entries.definition: a metal element, unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 钙，仅拼写相近，词源无关

entries.definition: lack of feeling or awareness
entries.definitionCN: 麻木；无感

entries.definition: lack of interest or emotion
entries.definitionCN: 冷漠；无动于衷

entries.definition: cruel disregard for others
entries.definitionCN: 冷酷无情

entries.definition: stubborn hardness of heart
entries.definitionCN: 顽固；冷酷

entries.definition: medical hardening of tissue
entries.definitionCN: （医学）组织硬化

normalIntro.en: Hands that grip forever grow the callosity that never feels.
normalIntro.cn: 永远紧握的手，会长出永不喊痛的茧。

normal.en: Latin callum means hard skin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 callum 意为硬皮。

normal.en: Callus is the medical word; callosity the literary one.
normal.cn: callus 是医学术语，callosity 偏文学。

normal.en: Callous the adjective means unfeeling.
normal.cn: 形容词 callous 意为冷酷的。

normal.en: Moral callosity is the figurative use.
normal.cn: moral callosity 是比喻用法。

normal.en: Calcium is unrelated despite the look.
normal.cn: calcium 与其拼写相近但词源无关。

abstract.en: Feel the smooth yellow ridge of a rower's palm.
abstract.cn: 感受船夫掌心那道光滑的黄茧。

abstract.en: See a refusal delivered with no flicker of feeling.
abstract.cn: 看一句拒绝说得毫无波澜。

abstract.en: Picture bark growing over a scarred trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象树皮盖住伤痕累累的树干。

examples.en: Blacksmith's callosities deepened with every forge year.
examples.cn: 铁匠的茧随每一年打铁而愈发厚实。

examples.en: The warden's moral callosity shocked the inspectors.
examples.cn: 典狱长的冷酷麻木令检查员震惊。

examples.en: A callosity formed along the healed fracture.
examples.cn: 愈合的骨折处长出了骨痂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「磕·老·茧」——手总「磕」在硬物上，时间久了就「老」出「茧」，与 callosity 的老茧义扣合。

root: callosity 源自拉丁语 callum「硬皮」加抽象后缀 -itas（callositas「硬化状态」）；本指磨出的老茧，延伸到骨痂，再借喻心灵的冷酷；同族词 callous、callus、callously 共享「硬」根。

sensesIntro.en: Skin hardened by labour, bone hardened in healing, and a heart hardened by habit.
sensesIntro.cn: 劳作磨硬的皮肤、愈合中变硬的骨骼，以及被习惯磨硬的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm whose skin has grown like bark.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心皮肤硬得像树皮。

branches.en: callosities from forty seasons of labour
branches.cn: 四十年劳作磨出的老茧

branches.en: the oarsman's hard palms
branches.cn: 桨手粗硬的手掌

branches.en: a callosity knitting the bone
branches.cn: 愈合处的骨痂

branches.en: moral callosity past shame
branches.cn: 不知羞耻的道德麻木

branches.en: the skin that feels nothing, the heart that feels nothing
branches.cn: 无知觉的皮肤与无知觉的心

intro.en: The Latin hard-skin stem call- carries into callus, callous, and callosity.
intro.cn: 拉丁「硬皮」词干 call- 贯穿 callus、callous 与 callosity。

latinIntro.en: Latin callum, hard skin, plus -itas gives callositas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 callum（硬皮）加 -itas 构成 callositas。

definition_zh: 文明的；有教养的；开化的；（口语）舒适宜人的
definition_en: having a refined and orderly way of life, or showing polite behaviour; informally, pleasant and comfortable
core_image: 一张铺着白布的长桌，杯碟成行，人们压低声音交谈
scene: 晚餐时无人高声争执，主人把餐具摆得整整齐齐，客人称这里像文明世界的一角。 No one raised a voice at dinner and the host laid every place neatly, so a guest called the house a corner of the civilized world.
sceneCN: 这里 civilized 指「举止有礼、生活有序的」（第 2 个义项：有教养的、讲礼的）；句意为晚餐时无人高声争执，主人把餐具摆得整齐，客人称这里像文明世界的一角。可辨识物件：白布长桌、成行杯碟、压低声音的客人、烛台。

pos.zh: 文明的；有教养的；开化的；（口语）舒适宜人的

senses.title: Socially developed, with cities and institutions
senses.titleCN: 拥有城市与制度的高度发展
senses.definition: belonging to a society with cities, writing and organised government
senses.definitionCN: 属于拥有城市、文字与有组织政府的社会
senses.example: The river basin held a civilized order long before the first kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 早在第一个王国出现之前，这个流域已有文明秩序。
senses.why: the participle carries the process of civilization into an adjective, marking a society that has gone through it.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词把「文明化」的过程带入形容词，标记已经走过这一过程的社会。

senses.title: Polite and considerate
senses.definition: behaving with restraint and courtesy toward others
senses.definitionCN: 以克制与礼貌对待他人
senses.example: They disagreed for an hour and remained civilized throughout.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争论了一个小时，全程仍保持有教养。
senses.why: the Latin adjective already meant 'polite', so the everyday sense is older than the archaeological one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词本就有「有礼」之义，因此日常义比考古义更古老。

senses.title: Refined in taste and manner
senses.definition: showing cultivated taste in food, dress, speech or surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 在饮食、穿着、言谈或环境上显示出修养
senses.example: The hotel served a civilized breakfast of fruit and strong coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店供应水果与浓咖啡，早餐颇为讲究。
senses.why: refinement is the visible trace of long training in restraint, which the adjective can mark.
senses.whyCN: 精致是长期克制训练的可见痕迹，这个形容词可以标记它。

senses.title: Pleasant and comfortable, informally
senses.definition: used lightly to mean agreeable, convenient or humane in ordinary arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 轻松用法，指日常安排中令人愉快、方便或合乎人情
senses.example: A civilized wait of ten minutes beats an hour in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 等十分钟这种体面的等待，好过在雨里站一小时。
senses.why: the colloquial sense borrows the moral word for small comforts, which is why it sounds faintly humorous.
senses.whyCN: 口语义把这个道德词借用于小舒适，因此听起来略带幽默。

senses.title: Humane treatment
senses.definition: showing that people or animals are treated with dignity rather than harshly
senses.definitionCN: 显示人或动物受到有尊严的对待，而非粗暴对待
senses.example: The report demanded civilized conditions for the prisoners.
senses.exampleCN: 报告要求为囚犯提供人道的条件。
senses.why: the word is used to set a floor of decency, implying that anything less is a lapse.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被用来设定体面的下限，暗示低于此即为失格。

senses.title: Settled life rather than wilderness
senses.definition: describing settled, built landscapes as opposed to wild or frontier conditions
senses.definitionCN: 描述已定居、已建设的环境，与荒野或边地相对
senses.example: Beyond the last fence the map stopped calling the land civilized.
senses.exampleCN: 越过最后一道栅栏，地图便不再称这片土地为文明之地。
senses.why: the old contrast between town and wilderness survives in travel writing and maps.
senses.whyCN: 城镇与荒野的古老对照在游记与地图中延续下来。

senses.title: A ranking of peoples, now contested
senses.titleCN: 曾被用来给人排序（今有争议）
senses.definition: the older use that ranked peoples as more or less civilized, now avoided in careful writing
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法把人按文明程度排序，如今在严谨写作中已被回避
senses.example: The old textbook called some peoples civilized and others savage.
senses.exampleCN: 旧教科书把一些民族称为文明，另一些称为野蛮。
senses.why: the ranking was an imperial assumption, and modern usage treats it as a judgement rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 这种排序是帝国时代的假设，现代用法视其为判断而非描述。

senses.title: Abstract: acceptable and decent
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：可接受、合体统的
senses.definition: used loosely of anything considered acceptable, orderly or decent
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地指任何被认为可接受、有序或体面的事物
senses.example: Ten in the morning is a civilized time to call, unlike six.
senses.exampleCN: 上午十点打电话是体面的时间，六点则不是。
senses.why: the abstraction keeps only the approval: what is civilized is what a reasonable person would accept.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法只保留「认可」这一层：文明的就是通情达理者能接受的。

intro.en: Civilized is civil plus the verb ending -ize and the past-participle -ed, modelled on French civiliser. Civil goes back to Latin civis 'citizen'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: civilized 是 civil 加动词词尾 -ize 与过去分词 -ed，仿法语 civiliser 构成。civil 可回溯到拉丁 civis「公民」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Civis 'citizen' is the root; its deeper origin is not established, and a connection with a root meaning 'to settle' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 词根是 civis「公民」；其更远来源未得到证明，与表示「定居」的词根相联系只是假说。

items.en: Civilis 'of citizens, polite' already paired urbanity with courtesy, the two ideas the English word still joins.
items.cn: civilis「公民的、有礼的」已把城市性与礼貌并置，英语词至今仍合着这两层。

items.en: Greek -izein and Latin -izare formed verbs meaning 'to make or become'; English -ize continues that pattern.
items.cn: 希腊 -izein 与拉丁 -izare 构成表示「使成为」的动词；英语 -ize 延续这一模式。

items.en: French civiliser meant to bring someone into a polite, settled way of life, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 civiliser 意为使某人进入有礼、定居的生活方式，英语于 16 世纪借入。

items.en: The participle was then used to rank peoples, a usage that later scholarship rejected as a value judgement.
items.cn: 这个分词随后被用于给民族排序，后来的学术研究将其视为价值判断而予拒斥。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest English citation is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of civis is unsettled, so any reconstructed root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：英语最早书证尚无定论，civis 在拉丁语之前的来源亦未确定，任何重构词根都是假说。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that are frequently swapped with the participle; group two holds other words for refinement and courtesy.
note.cn: 第一组是常与该分词互换的同根形式；第二组是表示精致与礼貌的其他词。

entries.definition: Means civic or polite, but makes no claim about social development; a civil reply is merely courteous.
entries.definitionCN: 指公民的或有礼的，但不涉及社会发展程度；仅表礼貌时也只说 civil，与文明程度无关。

entries.definition: The society or the process itself; civilized is the adjective describing what has gone through it.
entries.definitionCN: 指社会或过程本身；civilized 是形容已走过这一过程之物的形容词。

entries.definition: The same word spelled with -s-, standard in British English; the meaning is identical.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词的英式拼写，用 -s-，含义完全相同。

entries.definition: Relating to a city's government and public duties, not to manners or development.
entries.definitionCN: 与城市政府及公共职责有关，不涉及礼仪或发展程度。

entries.definition: From Latin politus 'polished': the plain word for good manners, with no historical scale attached.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 politus「打磨过的」：指有礼貌的日常词，不附带历史标尺。

entries.definition: Having learned taste in art and ideas; it stresses cultivation rather than social order.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术与思想上受过熏陶；强调修养，而非社会秩序。

entries.definition: Literally purified, as sugar or oil, and by extension delicate in manner; it stresses the removal of coarseness.
entries.definitionCN: 字面指被提纯，如糖或油，引申指举止细腻；强调去除粗糙。

entries.definition: From Latin urbanus 'of the city': smooth and sophisticated in manner, the polish of city life.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 urbanus「城市的」：举止圆熟老练，是城市生活的打磨。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Civilized is civil plus -ize plus -ed: something that has been made civil.
normal.cn: civilized 是 civil 加 -ize 再加 -ed：已被使得有礼有序之物。

normal.en: The Latin base already meant polite, which is why the everyday sense is the oldest.
normal.cn: 拉丁词基本就有「有礼」之义，因此日常义是最古老的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: civilized society, civilized behaviour, a civilized hour.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：文明社会、有教养的行为、体面的时刻。

normal.en: British spelling is civilised, with -s-, and the meaning does not change.
normal.cn: 英式拼写为 civilised，用 -s-，含义不变。

normal.en: Keep civil, civility and civilization apart: polite, politeness, and the society itself.
normal.cn: 把 civil、civility、civilization 分开：有礼、礼貌、社会本身。

abstract.en: Picture a long table with every glass placed at the same distance.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长桌，每只杯子摆在相同距离上。

abstract.en: Picture two people disagreeing in lowered voices.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人压低声音各持己见。

abstract.en: Picture a fence beyond which the map changes its word.
abstract.cn: 想象一道栅栏，越过它地图就换了一个词。

examples.en: A civilized argument leaves the other person's dignity intact.
examples.cn: 有教养的争论会让对方的尊严完好无损。

examples.en: The camp offered a civilized shower after ten days on the trail.
examples.cn: 在野外走了十天后，营地提供了相当体面的淋浴。

examples.en: Careful writers now avoid ranking peoples as more or less civilized.
examples.cn: 严谨的作者如今避免把民族按文明程度排序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「civil（有礼）+ ized（已……的）」——已经变得有礼有序 → 文明的

root: civil（拉丁 civilis「公民的、有礼的」，出自 civis「公民」）+ -ize + -ed，仿法语 civiliser。civis 的更深来源不确定。英语 civilized。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one adjective from the developed society to courtesy, cultivated taste, small comforts, humane treatment, settled land, the old ranking and finally everyday decency.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：从高度发展的社会，到礼貌、精致品味、小舒适、人道对待、定居之地、旧时排序，最后是日常体面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white-clothed table, evenly set, with voices kept low.
core.cn: 核心意象：铺白布的长桌，餐具整齐，说话压低。

branches.en: SETTLED ORDER: cities and fenced land mark where the adjective applies.
branches.cn: 定居秩序：城市与有栅栏的土地标出这个形容词的适用范围。

branches.en: VISIBLE REFINEMENT: courtesy and taste are the everyday traces of long training.
branches.cn: 可见的精致：礼貌与品味是长期训练的日常痕迹。

branches.en: SMALL COMFORTS: the moral word is lent to showers and reasonable hours.
branches.cn: 小舒适：这个道德词被借给淋浴与合理的时刻。

branches.en: A FLOOR OF DECENCY: humane treatment sets the minimum below which the word is refused.
branches.cn: 体面下限：人道对待设定最低线，低于此便不配此词。

branches.en: FROM RANKING TO APPROVAL: the old scale is rejected, leaving only 'acceptable to a reasonable person'.
branches.cn: 从排序到认可：旧标尺被拒斥，只剩「通情达理者可接受」。

intro.en: Civilized is built from a Latin adjective, a verb ending and a participle ending, all three of which recur across English.
intro.cn: civilized 由一个拉丁形容词、一个动词词尾与一个分词词尾构成，三者在英语中都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin civis and civilis build civil, civilian, civility and civilize; the ending -ize comes from Greek -izein through Latin -izare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 civis 与 civilis 构成 civil、civilian、civility 与 civilize；词尾 -ize 由希腊 -izein 经拉丁 -izare 而来。

items.example: Civil manners came from the city.

items.meaning: to bring into a settled polite order
items.meaningCN: 使进入有礼有序的状态
items.example: The school tried to civilize the frontier.
civilized means having been made civil.
items.exampleCN: civilized 意为已被使得有礼有序。

definition_zh: 制定；构想；明确表述；按配方配制
definition_en: to express an idea precisely, or to work out a plan, rule or product in a fixed form
core_image: 散在纸上的几条意见被写进一张带编号的配方单，每一行都有确定的分量与顺序
scene: 团队把几周的讨论写成一份可执行的方案，交给上级审批。 The team formulated a plan that could be carried out step by step.
sceneCN: 这里指把想法写成一份具体的行动方案（第 3 个义项：制定计划、政策或策略）；句意：团队制定了一份可以逐步执行的计划。

senses.title: To express an idea precisely
senses.definition: to state an idea in clear, exact words so that it can be examined
senses.definitionCN: 用清楚准确的语言说出一个想法，使其可被检验
senses.example: He formulated the problem in one short sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一句短话把问题精确表述出来。
senses.why: A formula is a fixed form, and to formulate is to put thought into such a form.
senses.whyCN: 配方或公式是一种固定格式，而制定表述就是把思想放进这种格式。

senses.title: To write a formula in symbols
senses.definition: in chemistry or mathematics, to write a relation or a compound in standard symbols
senses.definitionCN: 在化学或数学中，用标准符号写出一个关系或一种化合物
senses.example: The students formulated the equation for the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们写出了这个反应的方程式。
senses.why: Symbols are the most exact kind of fixed form, so the word fits mathematics most literally.
senses.whyCN: 符号是最精确的固定格式，因此这个词在数学里最为字面。

senses.title: To devise a plan or policy
senses.definition: to work out a course of action in a form that others can follow
senses.definitionCN: 把一套行动安排成别人可以照着做的形式
senses.example: The team formulated a plan that could be carried out step by step.
senses.exampleCN: 团队制定了一份可以逐步执行的计划。
senses.why: A plan must be given a shape before it can be shared, and giving it shape is the work of this verb.
senses.whyCN: 计划必须先有形状才能被共享，而给它形状正是这个动词的工作。

senses.title: To state a theory precisely
senses.definition: to put a hypothesis into a form that can be tested and criticized
senses.definitionCN: 把假说放进一种可以被检验与批评的形式
senses.example: Newton formulated laws that still describe ordinary motion.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿提出了至今仍能描述日常运动的定律。
senses.why: A theory that stays vague cannot be tested, so formulating it is the first condition of science.
senses.whyCN: 含糊的理论无法检验，因此把它精确表述是科学的第一条件。

senses.title: To prepare a product to a formula
senses.definition: to mix a medicine, a food or a material according to a fixed recipe
senses.definitionCN: 按照固定配方混合药物、食品或材料
senses.example: The lab formulated the cream for sensitive skin.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为敏感肌肤配出了这款乳霜。
senses.why: Here the formula is a recipe rather than an equation, and the verb means to make the mixture.
senses.whyCN: 这里的配方是食谱而不是方程，动词意为把混合物做出来。

senses.title: To frame a question or argument
senses.titleCN: 把问题或论证组织成形
senses.definition: to arrange a question or an argument so that its parts are clear and ordered
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或论证安排得部分清楚、次序分明
senses.example: A good interviewer formulates the next question from the answer just given.
senses.exampleCN: 好的采访者会根据刚得到的回答组织下一个问题。
senses.why: Thinking becomes visible when it is given an order, and the verb names that ordering.
senses.whyCN: 思想在被赋予次序时才变得可见，这个动词命名的是那个安排次序的动作。

senses.title: To draw up rules or regulations
senses.definition: to set out rules in an official and precise wording
senses.definitionCN: 用正式而精确的措辞写出规则
senses.example: The committee formulated the rules for the new grant.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会拟订了这项新资助的规则。
senses.why: Rules must be fixed in words before they can bind anyone, which is a formal version of formulation.
senses.whyCN: 规则必须先固定成文字才能约束人，这是「成形」的正式版本。

senses.title: To compose a response or statement
senses.definition: to prepare a reply or a public statement in careful wording
senses.definitionCN: 用审慎的措辞准备一份答复或公开声明
senses.example: The office formulated a short response to the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构对投诉拟定了一份简短回应。
senses.why: A response is an idea that must be given a public shape before it leaves the room.
senses.whyCN: 回应是一个必须先在室内成形、才能送出房间的想法。

intro.en: Formulate comes from the Latin noun for a small mould or a fixed pattern, and from a verb meaning to shape it. French passed the verb to English in the eighteenth century, and its senses spread from recipes to policies.
intro.cn: 本词出自拉丁语中表示小模子或固定格式的名词，以及一个意为按此成形的动词。法语在十八世纪把这个动词传给英语，含义从配方扩展到政策。

items.en: Forma meant shape, mould or pattern, and it stands behind the whole English family of form words.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指形状、模子或格式，英语中一整族与形式有关的词都出自它。

items.en: Formula was a small mould, and then a fixed wording or a set pattern.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词原指小模子，后来指固定的措辞或既定的格式。

items.en: The verb meant to shape something or to set it down in a fixed form.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为使成形，或按固定格式写下。

items.en: French carried the verb forward in the sense of putting an idea into exact words.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词推进到「把想法放进确切措辞」的意义。

items.en: English took it in the eighteenth century, when scientific and legal writing needed exact statements.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入，当时科学与法律写作都需要精确陈述。

items.en: Chemistry kept the recipe sense, while policy and management took the planning sense.
items.cn: 化学保留了配方义，政策与管理则取用了制定计划之义。

note.en: The first group shares the shape root or its English family; the second group names nearby kinds of putting ideas into form. Formulate stresses giving an idea a precise and workable shape, while facilitate stresses removing obstacles so that work can proceed.
note.cn: 第一组共享形状词根或其英语词族；第二组是相邻的「使想法成形」方式。本词强调给想法一个精确可用的形状，便利类词强调搬走障碍让工作得以前进。

entries.definition: A fixed set of symbols, a recipe or a worn phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 一组固定的符号、一份配方或一句套话。

entries.definition: The wording produced, and the act of producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 产生的措辞，以及产生它的动作。

entries.definition: Made to a fixed pattern, often in a negative sense of stale wording.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定格式做成，常含措辞陈旧之贬义。

entries.definition: The arrangement of a page or a file, from the same shape root.
entries.definitionCN: 页面或文件的排列方式，出自同一形状词根。

entries.definition: To invent or work out a plan; the emphasis is on invention, not exact wording.
entries.definitionCN: 发明或想出计划；强调发明，而非精确措辞。

entries.definition: To put a question or a statement into words; it stresses the frame around it.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题或陈述组织成话；强调外围框架。

entries.definition: To write a first version; it need not be precise yet.
entries.definitionCN: 写出初稿；此时还不必精确。

entries.definition: To express clearly in speech; it stresses clear delivery rather than planned form.
entries.definitionCN: 口头清楚表达；强调表达清楚，而非计划好的形式。

entries.definition: To put parts together into a whole, as in writing or music.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分组合成整体，如写作或音乐。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the shape root, the real family and the objects that show planning, science and recipes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用形状词根、真实同族词，以及能显示计划、科学与配方的宾语。

normal.en: The root means shape, and a small mould is inside the noun, so the verb means to give an idea a mould.
normal.cn: 词根意为形状，名词里含有一个小模子，因此动词意为给想法一个模子。

normal.en: The family runs formula, formulation, formulaic and formulator.
normal.cn: 同族词有公式、表述、公式化的与制定者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: formulate a plan, formulate a policy, formulate a theory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：制定计划、制定政策、提出理论。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps the literal recipe sense, and politics keeps the planning sense.
normal.cn: 化学保留字面的配方义，政治保留制定计划的义项。

normal.en: A statement that cannot be put into exact words has not yet been formulated.
normal.cn: 还不能被放进确切措辞的陈述，就还没有被制定成形。

abstract.en: Picture loose notes on a table being copied into numbered lines of a recipe card.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上散乱的笔记被抄进一张带编号的配方卡。

abstract.en: Picture a shapeless lump of clay pressed into a mould and coming out with edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一团没有形状的黏土被压进模子，出来时有了棱角。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of opinions reduced to one sentence everyone can read.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆意见被归结为每个人都能读到的一句话。

examples.en: The committee formulated a set of rules for the competition.
examples.cn: 委员会为这项比赛制定了一套规则。

examples.en: She formulated her objection in two precise sentences.
examples.cn: 她用两句精确的话表述了自己的反对意见。

examples.en: The company formulated a new fuel from plant waste.
examples.cn: 这家公司用植物废料配制出一种新燃料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛」加「缪」加「莱特」——把散乱的想法压进一个模子，出来就有棱有角：制定、表述

root: 拉丁语「形状、模子」衍生出「小模子、固定格式」，再加动词词尾构成「使成形」，经法语于十八世纪进入英语；由配方扩展到政策与理论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all give an idea a fixed shape: exact words, symbols, a plan, a theory, a recipe, a question, a rule and a public reply.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都给想法一个固定形状：准确措辞、符号、计划、理论、配方、问题、规则与公开答复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose notes on a table copied into a numbered recipe card, every line with a fixed amount and a fixed order.
core.cn: 核心意象：散在纸上的几条意见被写进一张带编号的配方单，每一行都有确定的分量与顺序。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: an idea put into exact words, and a question or an argument ordered.
branches.cn: 陈述：被放进准确措辞的想法，以及被安排好次序的问题或论证。

branches.en: THE SYMBOLS AND THE THEORY: an equation written, and a hypothesis made testable.
branches.cn: 符号与理论：写出的方程，以及变得可检验的假说。

branches.en: THE PLAN: a course of action shaped so that others can follow it.
branches.cn: 计划：成形后别人可以照着走的行动安排。

branches.en: THE RECIPE: a medicine, food or material mixed to a fixed formula.
branches.cn: 配方：按固定配方混合的药物、食品或材料。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL WORD: rules drawn up, and a reply carefully worded.
branches.cn: 正式文字：拟订的规则与措辞审慎的答复。

intro.en: Formulate is a Latin noun of shape turned into a verb, and its family supplies the formula, the wording and the adjective for stale patterns.
intro.cn: 本词是由一个表示形状的拉丁名词变成的动词，其词族提供公式、措辞，以及描述陈旧格式的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma and formula supply the core, and the verb ending was added first in Latin and then carried by French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示形状与小模子的两个名词提供核心，动词词尾先在拉丁语加上，再由法语带过来。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a fixed outline.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供固定轮廓的观念。

items.meaning: a small mould; a fixed wording
items.example: The noun is the direct base of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语词的直接基础。

items.meaning: to shape, to set in a form
items.example: The Latin verb supplies the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词提供动作。

items.example: French carried the verb into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个动词带进英语。

items.example: It gives the borrowed stem its English shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给借来的词干披上英语外形。

items.example: It builds the noun for the wording produced.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示所产生措辞的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for fixed, stale patterns.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述固定陈旧格式的形容词。

items.example: It builds the name of the person who draws up the formula.
The shortest descendant of the same root.

latinEntries.meaning: a small mould; a fixed form of words

definition_zh: n. 幽闭恐惧症；对封闭空间的强烈恐惧
definition_en: a strong fear of being in small or enclosed spaces
core_image: 电梯门合拢的一刻，胸口忽然收紧
scene: 电梯门一关上，她就感到一阵幽闭恐惧。 She felt a rush of claustrophobia as the lift doors closed.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：claustrophobia 指幽闭恐惧；句意是电梯门一关上，她就感到一阵幽闭恐惧。

derivatives.zh: 幽闭恐惧的；令人压抑的

senses.title: Fear of enclosed spaces
senses.definition: an intense fear of being in small or closed places
senses.definitionCN: 对狭小或封闭场所的强烈恐惧
senses.example: The tiny lift triggered her claustrophobia.
senses.exampleCN: 狭小的电梯引发了她的幽闭恐惧。
senses.why: Latin claustrum means an enclosed place and Greek phobos means fear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 claustrum 意为封闭处，希腊语 phobos 意为恐惧。

senses.title: A feeling of being trapped
senses.definition: a suffocating sense of being shut in by a situation
senses.definitionCN: 被某种处境困住的窒息感
senses.example: He felt a kind of claustrophobia in his narrow routine.
senses.exampleCN: 他在狭窄的日常里有一种被困住的压抑。
senses.why: Fear of closed rooms widened to closed lives.
senses.whyCN: 对封闭房间的恐惧扩展到了封闭的生活。

intro.en: The word joins a Latin room to a Greek fear and was coined for medicine.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语的「房间」和希腊语的「恐惧」结合，为医学而造。

items.en: Claustrum means a lock, a bolt or an enclosed place.
items.cn: claustrum 意为锁、门闩或封闭处。

items.en: Phobos means fear or panic.
items.cn: phobos 意为恐惧、惊惶。

items.en: Psychiatrists build the term for fear of closed rooms.
items.cn: 1879 年精神科医生造出此词，指对封闭房间的恐惧。

items.en: The word passes from clinics into daily speech.
items.cn: 二十世纪该词从诊所进入日常语言。

items.en: It now also names the feeling of a shut-in life.
items.cn: 现代也指被封闭生活困住的感觉。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -phobia shape; the near-meaning group names other phobias and fears.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -phobia 词形；近义组列出其他恐惧症与恐惧。

entries.definition: Fear of open or crowded places.
entries.definitionCN: 广场恐惧症。

entries.definition: Fear or dislike of foreigners.
entries.definitionCN: 排外恐惧。

entries.definition: Causing or feeling this fear.
entries.definitionCN: 引起幽闭恐惧的。

entries.definition: A strong unreasonable fear.
entries.definitionCN: 恐惧症。

entries.definition: A lasting feeling of worry.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑。

entries.definition: Great fear of something coming.
entries.definitionCN: 畏惧。

normalIntro.en: Claustrum is a closed room and phobos is fear: a room that frightens.
normalIntro.cn: claustrum 是封闭房间，phobos 是恐惧：一间吓人的屋子。

normal.en: Claustro means closed.
normal.cn: claustro 意为封闭。

normal.en: Phobia means fear.
normal.cn: phobia 意为恐惧。

normal.en: A lift is a moving closed room.
normal.cn: 电梯是会移动的封闭房间。

normal.en: The fear arrives when the doors shut.
normal.cn: 门一关，恐惧就来。

normal.en: The word can also picture a narrow life.
normal.cn: 这个词也能形容狭窄的生活。

abstract.en: Walls that move closer.
abstract.cn: 不断逼近的墙。

abstract.en: Fear with a locked door.
abstract.cn: 锁着门的恐惧。

abstract.en: Air that forgets to circulate.
abstract.cn: 忘了流动的空气。

examples.en: His claustrophobia makes tunnels difficult for him.
examples.cn: 他的幽闭恐惧让他难以忍受隧道。

examples.en: She stood near the exit to fight her claustrophobia.
examples.cn: 她站在出口附近，对抗自己的幽闭恐惧。

examples.en: The small village gave him a strange claustrophobia.
examples.cn: 这个小村庄让他有一种奇怪的被困感。

dict_mnemonic.text: claustro（封闭）+ phobia（恐惧）→ 对封闭空间的恐惧。

root: 拉丁 claustrum（封闭处）+ 希腊 phobos（恐惧）→ 医学新造词 claustrophobia

sensesIntro.en: A door that shuts becomes a metaphor for a life that closes.
sensesIntro.cn: 关上的门，成了封闭生活的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lift doors meeting in front of a face
core.cn: 核心意象：两扇电梯门在眼前合拢

branches.en: A lift door sliding shut.
branches.cn: 缓缓合上的电梯门。

branches.en: A tunnel with no light behind.
branches.cn: 身后无光的隧道。

branches.en: A small routine that will not open.
branches.cn: 打不开的狭小日常。

branches.en: A crowded room with no exit in sight.
branches.cn: 看不见出口的拥挤房间。

branches.en: A closed place and a closed life.
branches.cn: 封闭的场所与封闭的生活。

intro.en: Claustrophobia is built from a Latin room and a Greek fear; the list adds those pieces.
intro.cn: claustrophobia 由拉丁「房间」与希腊「恐惧」构成；下面列出这些成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin claustrum is a bolt, claudere is to shut, and Greek phobos is fear.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 claustrum 意为门闩，claudere 意为关闭，希腊语 phobos 意为恐惧。

latinEntries.exampleCN: claustrum 产生 claustrophobia 与 cloister。
claudere 产生 exclude 与 include。
phobos 产生 phobia 与 phobic。
